e.note: The Nine Tiele Tribes came to fight with over 100,000 men and sent out a few dozen of their bravest men to issue a challenge. Xue Rengui shot three arrows and killed three of them, and the rest dismounted and surrendered: "The general settled Tianshan with three arrows; the soldiers sing long songs as they march back through the Han passes." But Zheng Rentai advanced rashly and ran into heavy snow, and very many of his soldiers died of cold and hunger.
e.cmd: Zheng Rentai and Xue Rengui vs. the Nine Tiele Tribes

items.cmd: 刘仁轨、杜爽、扶余隆 vs 倭国援军、扶余丰
items.note: 唐水军一百七十艘列阵白江口，倭国援军争先进攻，唐军左右夹击，“四战捷，焚其舟四百艘，烟焰涨天，海水皆赤”；扶余丰逃往高句丽，周留城九月陷落。这是中日之间第一次大规模海战。

e.mod: mouth of the Geum River, South Korea
e.note: The Tang fleet of 170 ships drew up at the mouth of the Baek River. The Wa relief force rushed to attack, and the Tang struck them from both flanks: "four engagements, four victories; 400 of their boats burned; smoke and flames filled the sky, and the sea ran red". Buyeo Pung fled to Goguryeo, and Juryu Fortress fell in the 9th month. This was the first large-scale naval battle between China and Japan.
e.cmd: Liu Rengui, Du Shuang and Buyeo Yung vs. the Wa relief force and Buyeo Pung

items.cmd: 李勣 vs 高句丽
items.note: 李勣以新城为高句丽西境要冲，攻之，城人缚城主开门降；勣进击，周边十六城皆下，随后薛仁贵、庞同善击退泉男建援军。

e.note: Seeing Sinseong as the key point on Goguryeo's western border, Li Ji attacked it, and its people bound their commander and opened the gates in surrender; pressing on, he took all 16 towns around it. Xue Rengui and Pang Tongshan then drove off Yeon Namgeon's relief army.
e.cmd: Li Ji vs. Goguryeo

items.cmd: 薛仁贵 vs 高句丽
items.note: 薛仁贵以三千人攻扶余城，力战拔之，扶余川中四十余城望风请降。

e.note: Xue Rengui attacked Buyeo Fortress with 3,000 men and took it after hard fighting, and over 40 towns in the Buyeo valley surrendered at the news.
e.cmd: Xue Rengui vs. Goguryeo

items.sides: 唐·新罗 胜 高句丽
items.cmd: 李勣、薛仁贵、金仁问 vs 泉男建
items.note: 唐军与新罗军合围平壤月余，宝藏王与泉男产出降，泉男建闭城坚守，其将僧信诚开门内应，城破，高句丽亡。唐于其地置安东都护府，九都督府四十二州。

e.note: Tang and Silla forces besieged Pyongyang for over a month. King Bojang and Yeon Namsan came out and surrendered, but Yeon Namgeon shut the gates and held out until his general, the monk Sinseong, opened the gates from inside. The city fell, and Goguryeo came to an end. Tang set up the Andong Protectorate on its lands, with nine area commands and 42 prefectures.
e.sides: Tang and Silla defeated Goguryeo (city fell)
e.cmd: Li Ji, Xue Rengui and Kim In-mun vs. Yeon Namgeon

items.mod: 青海共和切吉草原一带
items.cmd: 论钦陵 vs 薛仁贵、郭待封
items.note: 唐军十余万（《旧唐书·高宗纪》作五万）护送吐谷浑复国，薛仁贵令郭待封留二万人于大非岭上立两栅守辎重，自率轻锐先趋乌海；郭待封违令，将辎重徐进，被吐蕃截击，辎重尽失；论钦陵率四十余万众合击，唐军大败，薛仁贵与吐蕃约和而还。

e.mod: around the Qieji Grassland, Gonghe, Qinghai
e.note: Over 100,000 Tang troops (50,000 in the "Annals of Gaozong" in the Old Book of Tang) were escorting the Tuyuhun to restore their state. Xue Rengui ordered Guo Daifeng to stay on Dafei Pass with 20,000 men and build two stockades to guard the baggage train, while he himself led lightly equipped picked troops ahead to Wuhai. Guo Daifeng disobeyed and moved slowly forward with the baggage; he was intercepted by the Tibetans and lost all of it. Gar Trinring then closed in with over 400,000 men, the Tang army was crushed, and Xue Rengui made peace with Tibet and withdrew.
e.yt: 8th month, 670 (7th month in the two Tang histories)
e.cmd: Gar Trinring vs. Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng

items.sides: 新罗 胜 唐（据《三国史记》；《新唐书》作唐胜）
items.cmd: 李谨行 vs 新罗军
items.note: 675 年李谨行率靺鞨等军屯买肖城，《三国史记》载新罗击走之、获战马三万余匹；《新唐书》则称李谨行三战皆捷。此后唐军在半岛渐失优势。

e.note: In 675 Li Jinxing camped at Maeso Fortress with Mohe and other troops. The Samguk sagi records that Silla drove him off and captured over 30,000 warhorses; the New Book of Tang, however, says that Li Jinxing won all three of his battles. After this the Tang army gradually lost the upper hand on the peninsula.
e.sides: Silla defeated Tang (per the Samguk sagi; the New Book of Tang has Tang victorious)
e.cmd: Li Jinxing vs. the Silla army

items.cmd: 施得 vs 薛仁贵
items.note: 新罗沙飡施得率水军与薛仁贵战于所夫里州伎伐浦，初战不利，此后大小二十二战，斩首四千余级（《三国史记》）。唐军退出半岛，罗唐战争结束。

e.mod: mouth of the Geum River, South Korea
e.note: Sideuk, a Silla official of sachan rank, led a fleet against Xue Rengui at Gibeolpo in Soburiju. The first engagement went against him, but in 22 battles large and small after that he took over 4,000 heads (per the Samguk sagi). The Tang army withdrew from the peninsula, and the Silla–Tang War came to an end.
e.cmd: Sideuk vs. Xue Rengui

items.cmd: 论钦陵 vs 李敬玄、刘审礼
items.note: 李敬玄率十八万众讨吐蕃，刘审礼前锋深入，于青海遇论钦陵大军，审礼被俘（一说战死），敬玄按兵不救，退屯承风岭；黑齿常之以敢死五百夜袭吐蕃营，唐军方得撤还。

e.note: Li Jingxuan led 180,000 men against Tibet. Liu Shenli's vanguard pushed deep and ran into Gar Trinring's main army at Qinghai Lake; Liu Shenli was captured (or killed in battle), while Li Jingxuan held his troops back and did not go to his rescue, falling back to camp at Chengfeng Pass. Only when Heichi Changzhi raided the Tibetan camp by night with 500 men sworn to die was the Tang army able to withdraw.
e.cmd: Gar Trinring vs. Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli

items.mod: 内蒙古呼和浩特北一带
items.sides: 唐 胜 突厥叛部
items.cmd: 裴行俭 vs 阿史那泥熟匐、奉职
items.note: 裴行俭率三十余万众讨突厥叛部，以粮车伏兵破其劫掠，三月大破之于黑山，擒奉职，泥熟匐为部下所杀。

e.mod: area north of Hohhot, Inner Mongolia
e.note: Pei Xingjian led over 300,000 men against the Turkic rebels. Hiding soldiers in grain wagons, he defeated their raiders, and in the 3rd month he crushed them at Heishan; Fengzhi was captured, and Nishufu was killed by his own followers.
e.cmd: Pei Xingjian vs. Ashina Nishufu and Fengzhi

items.mod: 吉尔吉斯斯坦伊塞克湖
items.sides: 唐 胜 西突厥余部
items.cmd: 王方翼 vs 车薄、咽面
items.note: 西突厥车薄、咽面围弓月城，安西都护王方翼引兵救之，战于热海，流矢贯臂而力战，大破之，擒其酋长三百人。

e.note: Chebo and Yanmian of the Western Turks besieged Gongyue City. Wang Fangyi, protector-general of Anxi, led troops to its relief and fought them at Issyk-Kul; with a stray arrow through his arm he fought on hard, crushed them and captured 300 of their chiefs.
e.sides: Tang defeated the Western Turkic remnants
e.cmd: Wang Fangyi vs. Chebo and Yanmian

items.cmd: 李孝逸、魏元忠 vs 徐敬业
items.note: 684 年九月徐敬业以匡复庐陵王为名起兵扬州，骆宾王作讨武曌檄；十一月李孝逸用魏元忠之计，乘风纵火，大破之于下阿溪，敬业逃至海陵被部下所杀。

e.note: In the 9th month of 684 Xu Jingye rose in arms at Yangzhou in the name of restoring the Prince of Luling, and Luo Binwang wrote the proclamation against Wu Zhao. In the 11th month Li Xiaoyi, following Wei Yuanzhong's plan, set fires with the wind behind him and crushed Xu Jingye at Xia'axi; Xu Jingye fled to Hailing, where he was killed by his own men.
e.cmd: Li Xiaoyi and Wei Yuanzhong vs. Xu Jingye

items.cmd: 黑齿常之 vs 骨咄禄、元珍
items.note: 后突厥寇朔州，燕然道大总管黑齿常之追击至黄花堆，大破之，突厥散走碛北。
items.yt: 687 年七月（《旧唐书·突厥传》作八月）

e.note: The Second Turks raided Shuozhou. Heichi Changzhi, commander-in-chief of the Yanran Route, pursued them to Huanghuadui and crushed them, and the Turks scattered north of the Gobi.
e.yt: 7th month, 687 (8th month in the "Turks" chapter of the Old Book of Tang)
e.cmd: Heichi Changzhi vs. Qutlugh and Yuanzhen

items.mod: 新疆伊犁一带（地望未定）
items.cmd: 吐蕃 vs 韦待价、阎温古
items.note: 韦待价为安息道大总管讨吐蕃，至寅识迦河，遇大雪，粮运不继，战败，士卒多冻馁而死，韦待价配流绣州。

e.note: Wei Daijia, as commander-in-chief of the Anxi Route, campaigned against Tibet. At the Yinshijia River he met heavy snow and his grain supplies could not keep up; he was defeated, and many of his soldiers died of cold and hunger. Wei Daijia was banished to Xiuzhou.
e.yt: 5th month, 689 (7th month in the Zizhi tongjian)
e.cmd: Tibet vs. Wei Daijia and Yan Wengu

items.cmd: 王孝杰、阿史那忠节 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 武威道总管王孝杰与阿史那忠节大破吐蕃，复取龟兹、于阗、疏勒、碎叶四镇；发汉兵三万镇守；其后言事者多请弃之，武则天不许（崔融上《拔四镇议》力主固守），四镇自此长期稳固。

e.note: Wang Xiaojie, commander of the Wuwei Route, and Ashina Zhongjie crushed the Tibetans and retook the Four Garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar and Suyab, and 30,000 Han troops were sent to garrison them. Afterwards many memorialists urged that they be abandoned, but Wu Zetian refused (Cui Rong submitted his "Discussion on Abandoning the Four Garrisons", arguing strongly that they be held). From then on the Four Garrisons remained secure for a long time.
e.cmd: Wang Xiaojie and Ashina Zhongjie vs. Tibet

items.mod: 新疆焉耆一带（地望未定）
items.sides: 唐 胜 吐蕃·西突厥
items.cmd: 王孝杰 vs 勃论赞刃、阿史那俀子
items.note: 王孝杰破吐蕃勃论赞刃、突厥可汗阿史那俀子等于冷泉及大岭，各三万余人；碎叶镇守使韩思忠又破泥熟俟斤等万余人。

e.note: Wang Xiaojie defeated the Tibetan Bolun Zanren, the Turkic qaghan Ashina Tuizi and others, each with over 30,000 men, at Lengquan and at Daling; Han Sizhong, garrison commissioner of Suyab, also defeated Nishu Irkin and others, with over 10,000 men.
e.sides: Tang defeated Tibet and the Western Turks
e.cmd: Wang Xiaojie vs. Bolun Zanren and Ashina Tuizi

items.cmd: 论钦陵、赞婆 vs 王孝杰、娄师德
items.note: 王孝杰、娄师德讨吐蕃，与论钦陵兄弟战于洮州素罗汗山，唐军大败，孝杰坐免为庶人，师德贬原州员外司马。

e.note: Wang Xiaojie and Lou Shide campaigned against Tibet and fought Gar Trinring and his brother at Mount Suluohan in Taozhou; the Tang army was crushed, Wang Xiaojie was dismissed and made a commoner for it, and Lou Shide was demoted to a supernumerary post at Yuanzhou.
e.cmd: Gar Trinring and Gar Tsenba vs. Wang Xiaojie and Lou Shide

items.cmd: 李尽忠、孙万荣 vs 曹仁师、张玄遇、麻仁节
items.note: 契丹以老弱诈降，诱唐军轻进，伏兵于黄獐谷，唐军大败，张玄遇、麻仁节被擒。

e.note: The Khitan sent their old and weak to feign surrender, luring the Tang army into a reckless advance, and laid an ambush in Huangzhang Valley. The Tang army was crushed, and Zhang Xuanyu and Ma Renjie were captured.
e.cmd: Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong vs. Cao Renshi, Zhang Xuanyu and Ma Renjie

items.cmd: 孙万荣 vs 王孝杰、苏宏晖
items.note: 王孝杰率十七万众讨契丹，至东硖石谷，前锋遇敌，苏宏晖畏敌先走，孝杰坠谷而死，唐军几乎全没。不久默啜袭契丹后方，孙万荣败死。

e.note: Wang Xiaojie led 170,000 men against the Khitan. At Dongxiashi Valley his vanguard met the enemy; Su Honghui, afraid of the enemy, fled first, Wang Xiaojie fell into a ravine and died, and the Tang army was almost entirely wiped out. Soon afterwards Qapaghan struck the Khitan from the rear, and Sun Wanrong was defeated and killed.
e.cmd: Sun Wanrong vs. Wang Xiaojie and Su Honghui

items.mod: 吉林长白山北麓一带（地望未定）
items.cmd: 大祚荣 vs 李楷固
items.note: 契丹降将李楷固追讨东走的靺鞨、高句丽余众，乞四比羽败死；大祚荣率众据天门岭迎击，大破唐军，遂东据东牟山建国。

e.mod: around the northern foot of the Changbai Mountains, Jilin (location uncertain)
e.note: Li Kaigu, a Khitan general who had surrendered, pursued the Mohe and Goguryeo remnants who were moving east, and Geolsa Biu was defeated and killed. Dae Joyeong led his people to hold Tianmenling against the attack and crushed the Tang army; he then went on east, held Mount Dongmou and founded his state.
e.cmd: Dae Joyeong vs. Li Kaigu

items.cmd: 唐休璟 vs 麹莽布支
items.note: 吐蕃麹莽布支寇凉州，陇右诸军州大使唐休璟与战于洪源谷，六战六胜，斩其副将二人、首二千五百级。

e.note: The Tibetan Qu Mangbuzhi raided Liangzhou. Tang Xiujing, grand commissioner of the armies and prefectures of Longyou, fought him at Hongyuan Valley and won six battles out of six, beheading two of his deputy generals and taking 2,500 heads.
e.cmd: Tang Xiujing vs. Qu Mangbuzhi

items.cmd: 默啜 vs 沙吒忠义
items.note: 默啜寇灵州鸣沙，灵武军大总管沙吒忠义逆战，败绩，死者六千余人（《旧唐书·中宗纪》作三万）；突厥进寇原、会等州，掠陇右牧马万余匹而去。

e.note: Qapaghan raided Mingsha in Lingzhou. Shazha Zhongyi, commander-in-chief of the Lingwu Jun, met him in battle and was defeated, with over 6,000 dead (30,000 in the "Annals of Zhongzong" in the Old Book of Tang). The Turks went on to raid Yuanzhou, Huizhou and other prefectures, and left with over 10,000 horses from the pastures of Longyou.
e.cmd: Qapaghan vs. Shazha Zhongyi

items.mod: 新疆拜城一带（地望未定）
items.cmd: 娑葛 vs 牛师奖
items.note: 突骑施娑葛因唐廷议立阿史那献、宗楚客受赂袭击之事，自立为可汗，发兵五道入寇；安西副都护牛师奖与战于火烧城，败没，娑葛遂陷安西。

e.note: Saqal of the Türgesh, because the Tang court had discussed setting up Ashina Xian and Zong Chuke had taken bribes to have him attacked, proclaimed himself qaghan and invaded along five routes. Niu Shijiang, deputy protector-general of Anxi, fought him at Huoshao City and was defeated and killed, and Saqal then took Anxi.
e.cmd: Saqal vs. Niu Shijiang

items.cmd: 李大酺 vs 孙佺
items.note: 幽州都督孙佺发兵二万、骑八千讨奚，至冷陉遇奚酋李大酺骑兵八千，唐军大败，孙佺被执，送默啜处被杀。

e.note: Sun Quan, area commander of Youzhou, set out against the Xi with 20,000 troops and 8,000 cavalry. At Lengxing he met 8,000 horsemen under the Xi chief Li Dapu; the Tang army was crushed, and Sun Quan was captured, handed over to Qapaghan and killed.
e.cmd: Li Dapu vs. Sun Quan

items.mod: 新疆吉木萨尔北庭故城
items.cmd: 郭虔瓘 vs 同俄特勤
items.note: 默啜遣其子同俄特勤围北庭，都护郭虔瓘出战，斩同俄于城下，突厥请以军资赎之，闻其已死，乃退。

e.note: Qapaghan sent his son Tong'e Tegin to besiege Beiting. The protector-general Guo Qianguan came out to fight and beheaded Tong'e beneath the walls; the Turks offered their army's supplies to ransom him, and on learning that he was already dead they withdrew.
e.cmd: Guo Qianguan vs. Tong'e Tegin

items.cmd: 薛讷、王晙 vs 坌达延、乞力徐
items.note: 吐蕃十万众寇临洮，进攻兰、渭，王晙夜袭吐蕃营，薛讷继之，大破于武街（新纪作武阶）、长城堡，杀获数万，洮水为之不流。

e.note: A Tibetan army of 100,000 raided Lintao and attacked Lanzhou and Weizhou. Wang Jun raided the Tibetan camp by night, Xue Ne followed up, and they crushed the Tibetans at Wujie (written with a different character in the New Book of Tang annals) and Changcheng Fort, killing or capturing tens of thousands, so that the Tao River stopped flowing.
e.cmd: Xue Ne and Wang Jun vs. Bendayan and Qilixu

items.mod: 乌兹别克斯坦费尔干纳盆地
items.cmd: 张孝嵩 vs 阿了达
items.note: 大食与吐蕃共立阿了达为拔汗那王，发兵攻其国，拔汗那王奔安西求救；监察御史张孝嵩率戎落兵万余人出龟兹数千里，攻下连城数百，阿了达逃入山谷，威震西域。

e.note: The Arab Caliphate and Tibet together set up Aliaoda as king of Ferghana and sent troops against the country, and the king of Ferghana fled to Anxi for help. The investigating censor Zhang Xiaosong led over 10,000 tribal troops several thousand li out from Kucha and took several hundred towns one after another; Aliaoda fled into the mountain valleys, and Zhang Xiaosong's might awed the Western Regions.
e.cmd: Zhang Xiaosong vs. Aliaoda

items.sides: 唐 发兵往击（胜负史缺）
items.cmd: 汤嘉惠、阿史那献 vs 苏禄
items.note: 突骑施苏禄引大食、吐蕃谋取四镇，围钵换及大石城；安西都护汤嘉惠奏已发三姓葛逻禄兵与阿史那献共击之，汉文史料未载胜负。

e.note: Suluk of the Türgesh brought in the Arab Caliphate and Tibet in a plan to seize the Four Garrisons, and besieged Bohuan and Dashi City. Tang Jiahui, protector-general of Anxi, reported that he had sent troops of the three tribes of the Karluks to attack them together with Ashina Xian; Chinese sources do not record the outcome.
e.cmd: Tang Jiahui and Ashina Xian vs. Suluk

items.cmd: 暾欲谷 vs 杨敬述
items.note: 唐约拔悉密、奚、契丹夹击后突厥，暾欲谷先袭拔悉密于北庭，尽俘其众；回师经赤亭，掠凉州羊马，河西节度使杨敬述遣兵追击，大败于删丹。

e.note: Tang arranged with the Basmyl, the Xi and the Khitan to attack the Second Turks from both sides. Tonyukuk first fell on the Basmyl at Beiting and captured all of them; on his way back he passed through Chiting and plundered the sheep and horses of Liangzhou. Yang Jingshu, military governor of Hexi, sent troops in pursuit, and they were crushed at Shandan.
e.cmd: Tonyukuk vs. Yang Jingshu

items.mod: 内蒙古鄂托克前旗一带
items.cmd: 王晙、张说 vs 康待宾、康愿子
items.note: 安置在河曲的六胡州粟特降户康待宾起事，众七万，进逼夏州；王晙、郭知运等平之，722 年康愿子再起，张说讨平，徙河曲六州残胡五万余口于中原。

e.mod: around Otog Front Banner, Inner Mongolia
e.note: Kang Daibin, of the surrendered Sogdian households settled in the Six Hu Prefectures in the Yellow River bend, rose in revolt with 70,000 followers and advanced on Xiazhou; Wang Jun, Guo Zhiyun and others put the rising down. In 722 Kang Yuanzi rose again and was put down by Zhang Yue, and over 50,000 of the remaining Hu of the six prefectures of the river bend were moved to the Central Plains.
e.cmd: Wang Jun and Zhang Yue vs. Kang Daibin and Kang Yuanzi

items.sides: 唐·小勃律 胜 吐蕃
items.cmd: 张思礼、没谨忙 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 吐蕃攻小勃律，夺其九城，小勃律王没谨忙求救于北庭；节度使张孝嵩遣疏勒副使张思礼率蕃汉步骑四千昼夜倍道驰援，与没谨忙夹击，大破吐蕃，复九城。

e.note: Tibet attacked Little Balur and seized nine of its towns, and Mojinmang, King of Little Balur, asked the Beiting Protectorate for help. The military governor Zhang Xiaosong sent Zhang Sili, deputy commissioner of Kashgar, with 4,000 tribal and Han infantry and cavalry, who hurried to the rescue day and night at double speed. Together with Mojinmang they attacked from both sides, crushed the Tibetans and recovered the nine towns.
e.sides: Tang and Little Balur defeated Tibet
e.cmd: Zhang Sili and Mojinmang vs. Tibet

items.cmd: 悉诺逻 vs 田元献、王寿
items.note: 吐蕃大将悉诺逻攻陷瓜州，执刺史田元献及河西节度使王君㚟之父王寿，毁城而去；王君㚟随后为回纥所杀，张守珪修复瓜州。

e.note: The Tibetan general Xinuoluo took Guazhou, seized the prefect Tian Yuanxian and Wang Shou, father of Wang Junchuo, military governor of Hexi, and left after destroying the city walls. Soon afterwards Wang Junchuo was killed by the Huihe (Uyghurs), and Zhang Shougui rebuilt Guazhou.
e.cmd: Xinuoluo vs. Tian Yuanxian and Wang Shou

items.sides: 唐 守住 突骑施·吐蕃
items.cmd: 赵颐贞 vs 苏禄、吐蕃
items.note: 突骑施苏禄与吐蕃赞普围安西城，安西副大都护赵颐贞击走之。

e.note: Suluk of the Türgesh and the Tibetan tsenpo besieged the city of Anxi; Zhao Yizhen, deputy grand protector-general of Anxi, drove them off.
e.sides: Tang held the city against the Türgesh and Tibet
e.cmd: Zhao Yizhen vs. Suluk and Tibet

items.cmd: 萧嵩、杜宾客 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 728 年七月吐蕃大将悉末朗寇瓜州，为刺史张守珪击走；八月吐蕃复入寇，河西节度使萧嵩遣副将杜宾客率强弩四千破之于祁连城下，斩首五千级。

e.note: In the 7th month of 728 the Tibetan general Ximolang raided Guazhou and was driven off by the prefect Zhang Shougui. In the 8th month Tibet raided again; Xiao Song, military governor of Hexi, sent his deputy general Du Binke with 4,000 strong crossbowmen, who defeated the Tibetans beneath the walls of Qilian City and took 5,000 heads.
e.cmd: Xiao Song and Du Binke vs. Tibet

items.cmd: 李祎 vs 吐蕃守军
items.note: 石堡城据险居要，为吐蕃侵扰河西、陇右的据点；朔方节度使信安王李祎引兵深入，急攻拔之，唐改名振武军，河陇诸军游弈拓境千余里。

e.note: Shibao Fortress, strongly sited at a key point, was Tibet's base for raids on Hexi and Longyou. Li Yi, Prince of Xin'an, military governor of Shuofang, led his army deep into Tibetan territory and took the fortress by storm. Tang renamed it Zhenwu Jun, and the patrols of the armies of Hexi and Longyou pushed the frontier out by over 1,000 li.
e.cmd: Li Yi vs. the Tibetan garrison

items.cmd: 张文休 vs 韦俊
items.note: 渤海王大武艺因弟大门艺奔唐、唐置黑水都督府等事怨唐，遣大将张文休率海贼渡海袭登州，杀刺史韦俊。

e.note: Resenting Tang over the flight of his younger brother Dae Munye to Tang, the founding of the Heishui Area Command and other matters, Dae Muye, King of Balhae, sent his general Jang Munhyu with pirates across the sea to attack Dengzhou, and they killed the prefect Wei Jun.
e.cmd: Jang Munhyu vs. Wei Jun

items.sides: 契丹·突厥 胜 唐
items.cmd: 可突于 vs 郭英杰
items.note: 幽州副总管郭英杰与契丹可突于战于都山，可突于引突厥兵来援，唐军所部奚众持两端，郭英杰战死，所部六千余人尽没。

e.note: Guo Yingjie, deputy commander of Youzhou, fought Ketuyu of the Khitan at Mount Du. Ketuyu brought in Turkic troops to his aid, and the Xi serving with the Tang army wavered between the two sides; Guo Yingjie was killed in battle, and all of his more than 6,000 men were lost.
e.sides: Khitan and the Turks defeated Tang
e.cmd: Ketuyu vs. Guo Yingjie

items.cmd: 乌承玼 vs 大武艺
items.note: 渤海王大武艺率兵至马都山，屠陷城邑；平卢先锋乌承玼塞要道，堑以大石，亘四百里，渤海兵不得进，流民得以归。

e.note: Dae Muye, King of Balhae, led his army to Mount Madu, taking towns and massacring their people. Wu Chengci, commander of the Pinglu vanguard, blocked the key routes, barricading them with great stones along a line of 400 li; the Balhae troops could not advance, and the refugees were able to return home.
e.cmd: Wu Chengci vs. Dae Muye

items.cmd: 崔希逸 vs 乞力徐
items.note: 河西节度使崔希逸受命袭吐蕃，深入二千余里，破之于青海西，赤岭之盟遂坏；希逸以背约自愧，次年忧死。

e.note: Ordered to make a surprise attack on Tibet, Cui Xiyi, military governor of Hexi, drove over 2,000 li deep and defeated the Tibetans west of Qinghai Lake, and with that the Covenant of Chiling was broken. Ashamed at having broken the agreement, Cui Xiyi died of grief the next year.
e.cmd: Cui Xiyi vs. Qilixu

items.cmd: 杜希望 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 鄯州都督杜希望攻拔吐蕃新城，以其地为威戎军，置兵一千戍之。

e.note: Du Xiwang, area commander of Shanzhou, stormed the Tibetan town of Xincheng, made it Weirong Jun and stationed 1,000 troops there to hold it.
e.cmd: Du Xiwang vs. Tibet

items.mod: 吉尔吉斯斯坦托克马克
items.cmd: 盖嘉运、夫蒙灵察 vs 吐火仙、黑姓可汗
items.note: 碛西节度使盖嘉运率石国、史国等兵破突骑施吐火仙可汗于碎叶城下，追擒之；疏勒镇守使夫蒙灵察与拔汗那王袭怛逻斯，擒（《新唐书》作斩）黑姓可汗尔微，突骑施自此衰落。

e.note: Gai Jiayun, military governor of Qixi, with troops from Chach, Kesh and other states, defeated Tuhuoxian Qaghan of the Türgesh beneath the walls of Suyab, pursued him and captured him. Fumeng Lingcha, garrison commissioner of Kashgar, and the king of Ferghana made a surprise attack on Talas and captured (the New Book of Tang says beheaded) Erwei, the Black Clan Qaghan. From then on the Türgesh declined.
e.cmd: Gai Jiayun and Fumeng Lingcha vs. Tuhuoxian and the Black Clan Qaghan

items.cmd: 章仇兼琼 vs 吐蕃守军
items.note: 安戎城 680 年为吐蕃所陷，据险以逼蜀西；剑南节度使章仇兼琼密结城中翟都局等为内应，开门纳唐军，尽杀吐蕃将士，唐改名平戎城。

e.note: Anrong City had fallen to Tibet in 680, and from this strong position the Tibetans threatened western Shu. Zhangchou Jianqiong, military governor of Jiannan, secretly won over Zhai Duju and others in the city to work for him from inside; they opened the gates to the Tang army, and all the Tibetan officers and men were killed. Tang renamed it Pingrong City.
e.cmd: Zhangchou Jianqiong vs. the Tibetan garrison

items.mod: 青海贵德一带（地望未定）
items.cmd: 皇甫惟明 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 陇右节度使皇甫惟明深入吐蕃境，破其洪济城。

e.note: Huangfu Weiming, military governor of Longyou, drove deep into Tibetan territory and took Hongji City.
e.cmd: Huangfu Weiming vs. Tibet

items.cmd: 王忠嗣 vs 阿波达干
items.note: 朔方节度使王忠嗣乘后突厥内乱，大破其左厢阿波达干等十一部于萨河内山。

e.note: Taking advantage of civil strife among the Second Turks, Wang Zhongsi, military governor of Shuofang, crushed eleven tribes of their Left Wing, including Apa Tarqan's, at Mount Sahenei.
e.cmd: Wang Zhongsi vs. Apa Tarqan

items.cmd: 高仙芝、李嗣业 vs 吐蕃守军
items.note: 高仙芝分兵三道会于吐蕃连云堡下，郎将李嗣业持旗率陌刀手攀山先登，大破吐蕃，斩五千级；随后越坦驹岭，入阿弩越城，擒小勃律王，断藤桥以绝吐蕃援兵。

e.note: Gao Xianzhi divided his army into three columns, which converged beneath Lianyun Fort, held by Tibet. The commandant Li Siye, holding a banner, led the modao swordsmen up the mountainside and was first onto the walls; the Tibetans were crushed and 5,000 heads taken. Gao Xianzhi then crossed the Darkot Pass, entered Anuyue City, captured the king of Little Balur and cut the rattan bridge to block Tibetan reinforcements.
e.cmd: Gao Xianzhi and Li Siye vs. the Tibetan garrison

items.cmd: 哥舒翰 vs 悉诺罗
items.note: 石堡城 741 年复陷吐蕃；陇右节度使哥舒翰率陇右、河西、朔方、河东与突厥阿布思兵六万三千攻之，数日而拔，擒吐蕃铁刃悉诺罗等四百人，唐士卒死者数万，王忠嗣先前“以数万人争一城”之谏遂应。

e.note: Shibao Fortress had fallen to Tibet again in 741. Geshu Han, military governor of Longyou, attacked it with 63,000 troops from Longyou, Hexi, Shuofang and Hedong and the Turk Abusi's men, and took it after several days, capturing 400 Tibetans, including Xinuoluo of Tieren. Tens of thousands of Tang soldiers died, bearing out Wang Zhongsi's earlier warning against "fighting over one city with tens of thousands of men".
e.cmd: Geshu Han vs. Xinuoluo

items.cmd: 阁罗凤 vs 鲜于仲通
items.note: 剑南节度使鲜于仲通率兵八万分道讨南诏，阁罗凤遣使谢罪请和，不许；唐军进至西洱河，大败，士卒死者六万，仲通仅以身免。南诏从此北臣吐蕃。

e.note: Xianyu Zhongtong, military governor of Jiannan, led 80,000 troops along separate routes against Nanzhao. Geluofeng sent envoys to apologize and ask for peace, but was refused. The Tang army advanced to the Xi'er River and was crushed, with 60,000 soldiers dead; Xianyu Zhongtong barely escaped with his life. From then on Nanzhao turned north and became a vassal of Tibet.
e.cmd: Geluofeng vs. Xianyu Zhongtong

items.cmd: 齐雅德 vs 高仙芝
items.note: 石国王子引大食兵欲攻四镇，高仙芝率蕃汉三万深入七百余里，至怛罗斯城与大食军相持五日，葛逻禄部众倒戈，与大食夹击，唐军大败，仅数千人生还。被俘的杜环后作《经行记》。
items.yt: 751 年七月（据阿拉伯史料；《通鉴》系于四月条下）

e.note: The prince of Chach brought in troops of the Arab Caliphate, intending to attack the Four Garrisons. Gao Xianzhi pushed over 700 li deep with 30,000 tribal and Han troops; at the city of Talas he faced the Caliphate army for five days, until the Karluks turned against him and attacked from both sides together with the Caliphate forces. The Tang army was crushed, and only a few thousand men came back alive. Du Huan, who was taken prisoner, later wrote the Jingxing ji.
e.yt: 7th month, 751 (per Arabic sources; the Zizhi tongjian places it under the 4th month)
e.cmd: Ziyad ibn Salih vs. Gao Xianzhi

items.cmd: 契丹 vs 安禄山
items.note: 安禄山率幽州、云中、平卢、河东兵六万讨契丹，以奚为向导，至土护真水，遇雨，又昼夜兼行三百余里至契丹牙帐，弓弩筋胶皆弛，奚复叛，唐军大败，安禄山仅以二十骑逃归。

e.note: An Lushan led 60,000 troops from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu and Hedong against the Khitan, with the Xi as guides. At the Tuhuzhen River they met rain, and then marched day and night for over 300 li to the Khitan royal camp; the sinews and glue of their bows and crossbows had all slackened, and the Xi turned against them again. The Tang army was crushed, and An Lushan escaped with only 20 horsemen.
e.cmd: Khitan vs. An Lushan

items.cmd: 哥舒翰 vs 吐蕃
items.note: 陇右节度使哥舒翰击吐蕃，拔洪济、大漠门等城，悉收九曲部落；次年以其地置洮阳、浇河二郡与神策军、宛秀军。
items.yt: 753 年夏（新纪作 754 年三月）

e.note: Geshu Han, military governor of Longyou, attacked Tibet, took Hongji, Damomen and other towns, and brought all the tribes of Jiuqu under his control. The next year Taoyang and Jiaohe Commanderies and the Shence Jun and Wanxiu Jun were set up on these lands.
e.yt: summer 753 (3rd month, 754 in the New Book of Tang annals)
e.cmd: Geshu Han vs. Tibet

items.cmd: 封常清 vs 大勃律
items.note: 安西节度使封常清率兵击大勃律，至贺萨劳城，一战而胜，大勃律请降。

e.note: Feng Changqing, military governor of Anxi, led troops against Great Balur. At Hesalao City he won in a single battle, and Great Balur asked to surrender.
e.cmd: Feng Changqing vs. Great Balur

items.cmd: 阁罗凤 vs 李宓
items.note: 侍御史、剑南留后李宓率兵七万再讨南诏，至太和城，南诏闭壁不战，唐军粮尽，士卒罹瘴疫、饥饿死者十之七八，退军时为南诏所击，李宓被擒（新纪作死之），全军覆没。

e.note: Li Mi, attendant censor and acting military governor of Jiannan, led 70,000 troops in a second campaign against Nanzhao. At Taihe City Nanzhao kept behind its walls and refused battle; the Tang army ran out of food, and seven or eight in ten of its soldiers died of miasmal disease and hunger. As the army withdrew it was attacked by Nanzhao; Li Mi was captured (the New Book of Tang annals says he was killed), and the whole army was wiped out.
e.cmd: Geluofeng vs. Li Mi

items.note: 关中东大门。617 年屈突通据潼关拒李渊，兵败东走被擒；李建成随即屯守，关中尽入唐手。

e.note: The eastern gateway of Guanzhong. In 617 Qutu Tong held Tong Pass against Li Yuan; defeated, he fled east and was captured. Li Jiancheng then garrisoned the pass, and all of Guanzhong fell into Tang hands.

items.note: 黄河蒲津渡口，连通关中与河东。隋末尧君素据河东城为隋坚守，至 618 年十二月被部下所杀，其部将王行本 620 年方降唐。

e.note: The Pujin crossing of the Yellow River, linking Guanzhong with Hedong. In the late Sui Yao Junsu held Hedong City for the Sui to the last, until he was killed by his own men in the 12th month of 618; his officer Wang Xingben surrendered to Tang only in 620.

items.note: 长安东南门户，经商州通往南阳、襄阳。

e.note: The southeastern gateway of Chang'an, leading via Shangzhou to Nanyang and Xiangyang.

items.note: 秦岭北口，扼陈仓道入汉中、蜀中。

e.note: The northern entrance to the Qinling Mountains, commanding the Chencang Road into Hanzhong and Shu.

items.note: 又名大震关，翻越陇山的要道，关中与陇右的分界。

e.note: Also called Dazhen Pass; the main route over the Long Mountains and the boundary between Guanzhong and Longyou.

items.note: 关中西北门户，原州之东，扼泾水上游通往陇右、河西的大道。

e.note: The northwestern gateway of Guanzhong, east of Yuanzhou, commanding the main road along the upper Jing River to Longyou and Hexi.

items.note: 金牛道上的天险，“一夫当关，万夫莫开”；618 年巴蜀归唐，即由此道传檄。

e.note: A natural stronghold on the Jinniu Road: "one man holding the pass can stop ten thousand". In 618 Ba and Shu came over to Tang through proclamations sent along this road.

items.note: 长江三峡西口，夔州（白帝城）在此。621 年九月李孝恭、李靖率巴蜀舟师自此东下灭萧铣。

e.note: The western entrance to the Three Gorges of the Yangtze, where Kuizhou (Baidicheng) stood. In the 9th month of 621 Li Xiaogong and Li Jing led the Ba and Shu fleet downriver from here to destroy Xiao Xian.

items.note: 洛阳东门户，又称汜水关、成皋，北临黄河、南连嵩山。621 年李世民据此阻止窦建德西援，一战擒之。

e.note: The eastern gateway of Luoyang, also called Sishui Pass or Chenggao, with the Yellow River to the north and Mount Song to the south. In 621 Li Shimin held it to stop Dou Jiande from marching west to the rescue, and captured him in a single battle.

items.note: 太行陉上的关隘，连接泽州与河内。

e.note: A pass on the Taihang Defile, linking Zezhou with Henei.

items.note: 又称土门关，太行八陉之一，连接河东并州与河北恒州。

e.note: Also called Tumen Pass; one of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, linking Bingzhou in Hedong with Hengzhou in Hebei.

items.note: 太行八陉之一，代北通往易州、定州的孔道。

e.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang; the passage from Daibei to Yizhou and Dingzhou.

items.note: 唐称西陉关，河东北面屏障，615 年突厥始毕可汗即由此南下围炀帝于雁门郡城。

e.note: Called Xijing Pass under the Tang; the northern shield of Hedong. In 615 the Turkic Shibi Qaghan came south through here and besieged Emperor Yang of Sui in the seat of Yanmen Commandery.

items.note: 太行八陉之军都陉，幽州北门。

e.note: The Jundu Defile of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang; the northern gate of Youzhou.

items.note: 幽州东北通往奚、契丹的要道。

e.note: The main route from Youzhou northeast to the Xi and the Khitan.

items.note: 又作临渝关，辽西走廊西端，598 年汉王杨谅、612 年后隋军征高句丽皆出此关。

e.note: Also written Linyu Pass; at the western end of the Liaoxi corridor. Yang Liang, Prince of Han, in 598 and the Sui armies attacking Goguryeo from 612 on all went out through this pass.

items.note: 五岭之一，岭南与中原间最重要的通道，北江、赣江由此水陆相接。

e.note: One of the Five Ridges and the most important route between Lingnan and the Central Plains; here a land route linked the waterways of the Bei River and the Gan River.

items.note: 隋唐玉门关在瓜州晋昌城东，629 年（一说 627 年）玄奘西行即由此偷渡出关，北行莫贺延碛至伊吾。

e.note: The Sui–Tang Yumen Pass lay east of Jinchang City in Guazhou. In 629 (or 627) Xuanzang, traveling west, slipped out past it in secret, then went north across the Moheyan Desert to Yiwu.

items.note: 沙州西南出西域南道之关。

e.note: The pass southwest of Shazhou leading out onto the southern route through the Western Regions.

items.note: 焉耆通往龟兹道上的峡谷关隘。

e.note: A gorge pass on the road from Karasahr to Kucha.

items.note: 吐蕃称铁刃城，在赤岭之东二十里、湟水上游的山巅，三面绝壁，扼河陇入青海之路。729 年李祎引兵深入急攻拔之，改名振武军；741 年复陷吐蕃；749 年哥舒翰以六万余众攻之，死者数万方拔，改名神武军。

e.note: The Tibetans called it Tieren City. It stood on a mountaintop 20 li east of Chiling, on the upper Huangshui, with sheer cliffs on three sides, commanding the road from Hexi and Longyou into Qinghai. In 729 Li Yi led his troops deep into enemy country and took the fortress by a swift assault, and it was renamed Zhenwu Jun; in 741 it fell to Tibet again; in 749 Geshu Han attacked it with over 60,000 men and took it only after tens of thousands had died, and it was renamed Shenwu Jun.

items.note: 穿越阴山的南北孔道，白道川在其北。583 年隋破突厥、630 年李靖袭颉利、641 年李勣追薛延陀皆经此道。

e.note: A north–south thoroughfare across the Yin Mountains, with the Baidao Plain to its north. The Sui defeat of the Turks in 583, Li Jing's raid on Illig in 630 and Li Ji's pursuit of the Xueyantuo in 641 all went this way.

items.mod: 乌兹别克斯坦拜孙山口
items.note: 河中与吐火罗之间的峡谷隘口，两侧石壁色如铁，玄奘称“铁门”，为西突厥统叶护南境之关。

e.note: A gorge pass between Transoxiana and Tokharistan, its rock walls on both sides the color of iron; Xuanzang called it the "Iron Gate". It was the pass on the southern border of the Western Turks under Tong Yabghu.

items.note: 隋唐东征高句丽的集结地之一，645 年李勣自柳城佯出怀远镇，潜师北趋甬道渡辽水。

e.note: One of the assembly points for the Sui and Tang campaigns east against Goguryeo; in 645 Li Ji set out from Liucheng, feinting toward Huaiyuan Garrison, then marched north in secret toward Yongdao and crossed the Liao River.

items.mod: 内蒙古乌拉特中旗乌加河镇西南（一说临河高油坊古城）
items.note: 708 年张仁愿乘默啜西击突骑施，于黄河以北筑三受降城，西城在丰州西北，与中城相距三百八十里，自此突厥不敢度山畋牧。

e.mod: south-west of Wujiahe, Urad Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia (another view: Gaoyoufang site, Linhe)
e.note: In 708, while Qapaghan was attacking the Türgesh in the west, Zhang Renyuan built the Three Shouxiang Cities north of the Yellow River. The western city lay northwest of Fengzhou, 380 li from the central city; from then on the Turks no longer dared to cross the mountains to hunt and graze.

items.mod: 内蒙古包头南（一说达拉特旗二狗湾古城）
items.note: 三受降城之中城，即筑于拂云祠（拂云堆，突厥南侵前祭祀之所）故地，安北都护府后亦寄治于此。

e.mod: south of Baotou, Inner Mongolia (another view: Ergouwan site, Dalad Banner)
e.note: The central one of the Three Shouxiang Cities, built on the site of the Fuyun shrine (Fuyun Mound, where the Turks made sacrifices before raiding the south); the Anbei Protectorate was later also temporarily seated here.

items.note: 三受降城之东城，在胜州东北的黄河北岸；于牛头朝那山北置烽候千八百所。

e.note: The eastern one of the Three Shouxiang Cities, on the north bank of the Yellow River northeast of Shengzhou. North of Mount Niutouchaona 1,800 beacon posts were set up.

items.note: 北周静帝年幼，外戚杨坚以丞相总揽朝政，平定尉迟迥等三方起兵后受禅称帝，国号隋（取“随国公”之“随”去辵），年号开皇。

e.note: Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou was a child, and Yang Jian, an imperial in-law, controlled the government as chancellor. After putting down the risings on three fronts led by Yuchi Jiong and others, he accepted the abdication and proclaimed himself emperor. He named his dynasty Sui (taking the character for Sui from his title "Duke of Sui" and dropping its "walk" radical), with the era name Kaihuang.

items.note: 宇文恺规划，九个月建成宫城与皇城，583 年三月迁入。城市方正如棋盘，东西两市，为唐长安城的前身。

e.note: Planned by Yuwen Kai, the palace city and the imperial city were built in nine months, and the court moved in in the 3rd month of 583. The city was square and laid out like a chessboard, with an Eastern and a Western Market. It was the forerunner of Tang Chang'an.

items.note: 581 年颁行新律，583 年再加删订为十二篇五百条，废除枭首、车裂等酷刑，确立笞、杖、徒、流、死五刑，为唐律的蓝本。

e.note: A new code was issued in 581 and in 583 revised and pruned into 12 sections and 500 articles. It abolished cruel punishments such as exposing severed heads and dismemberment by chariots, and fixed the Five Punishments: beating with the light stick, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, exile and death. It became the model for the Tang Code.

items.mod: 新疆准噶尔一带（金山以西）
items.note: 长孙晟“远交近攻、离强合弱”，隋分化沙钵略、阿波、达头诸可汗；583 年阿波西奔达头，突厥自此分为东西两部。

e.old: The Turks split east and west
e.mod: around Dzungaria, Xinjiang (west of the Altai)
e.note: Following Zhangsun Sheng's policy of "befriending the distant and attacking the near, dividing the strong and uniting the weak", Sui set Ishbara, Apa, Tardu and the other qaghans against one another. In 583 Apa fled west to Tardu, and from then on the Turks were divided into eastern and western halves.

items.note: 隋征后梁主萧琮入朝，其叔父萧岩等挟江陵军民十余万投陈；隋废后梁，以江陵为荆州。

e.note: Sui summoned the Later Liang ruler Xiao Cong to court; his uncle Xiao Yan and others took over 100,000 soldiers and civilians of Jiangling with them and defected to Chen. Sui abolished Later Liang and made Jiangling into Jingzhou.

items.note: 岭南俚人首领冼夫人闻陈亡，率众迎接隋使韦洸，岭南诸州归隋；次年又平定王仲宣之乱，被封为谯国夫人。

e.note: On hearing that Chen had fallen, Lady Xian, leader of the Li people of Lingnan, led her followers to welcome the Sui envoy Wei Guang, and the prefectures of Lingnan submitted to Sui. The next year she also put down Wang Zhongxuan's rising, and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Qiao.

items.note: 杨素监造，役死者以万计，595 年建成；文帝晚年常居于此，604 年七月病逝于宫中大宝殿。唐改称九成宫，魏征撰《九成宫醴泉铭》。

e.note: Built under Yang Su's supervision at the cost of tens of thousands of laborers' lives, it was completed in 595. Emperor Wen often stayed here in his later years and died of illness in its Dabao Hall in the 7th month of 604. The Tang renamed it the Jiucheng Palace, and Wei Zheng wrote the Inscription on the Sweet Spring of the Jiucheng Palace (Jiuchenggong liquan ming).

items.note: 史万岁率军入南中，渡西洱河、过滇池，至“南中八十余部”，爨翫降服；隋于其地置南宁州总管，不久复叛。

e.note: Shi Wansui led an army into Nanzhong, crossed the Xi'er River and passed Lake Dian, reaching the "more than 80 tribes of Nanzhong", and Cuan Wan submitted. Sui set up the Nanning Zhou Area Command there, but the region soon rebelled again.

items.note: 高句丽王高元率靺鞨万余骑侵辽西，文帝命汉王杨谅、高颎率三十万出临渝关，周罗睺率水军自东莱泛海，陆军遇雨疫、水军遭风暴，死者十之八九而还。

e.note: Go Won, king of Goguryeo, led over 10,000 Mohe horsemen in a raid on Liaoxi. Emperor Wen ordered Yang Liang, Prince of Han, and Gao Jiong to lead 300,000 men out through Linyu Pass, while Zhou Luohou took the fleet by sea from Donglai. The land army met rain and disease and the fleet met storms; eight or nine in ten died, and the expedition returned.

items.note: 东突厥突利可汗娶隋安义公主，被都蓝可汗攻破后南投隋朝，隋拜为意利珍豆启民可汗，在朔州筑大利城以居其众。

e.old: Qimin comes south to submit · Dali City built
e.note: Tuli Qaghan of the Eastern Turks, who had married the Sui Princess Anyi, was crushed by Dulan Qaghan and fled south to Sui. Sui invested him as Yili Zhendou Qimin Qaghan and built Dali City in Shuozhou to house his people.

items.note: 匠人李春设计建造的单孔敞肩石拱桥（安济桥），跨洨河，主拱跨径约 37 米，两肩各开两小拱，是现存最古老的敞肩石拱桥。

e.note: A single-span open-spandrel stone arch bridge (the Anji Bridge), designed and built by the craftsman Li Chun, crossing the Xiao River. The main arch spans about 37 meters, with two small arches opened in each spandrel. It is the oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge.

items.note: 文帝病重于仁寿宫，太子杨广与杨素密谋，文帝崩，杨广即位；废太子杨勇被缢杀。宫变细节史家多有疑议。

e.note: Emperor Wen fell gravely ill at the Renshou Palace. The crown prince Yang Guang plotted in secret with Yang Su; Emperor Wen died and Yang Guang took the throne, and the deposed crown prince Yang Yong was strangled. Historians have raised many doubts about the details of the palace incident.

items.note: 炀帝诏杨素、宇文恺营建东京，每月役丁二百万，迁洛阳郭内居民及天下富商大贾数万户以实之，又于城内建含嘉仓，城外建回洛、洛口等大仓。

e.note: Emperor Yang ordered Yang Su and Yuwen Kai to build the Eastern Capital. Two million laborers worked on it every month, and the residents within the outer walls of Luoyang, along with tens of thousands of households of rich merchants from across the realm, were moved in to populate it. The Hanjia Granary was also built inside the city, and great granaries such as Huiluo and Luokou outside it.

items.note: 炀帝北巡至榆林，宇文恺造可容数百人的“观风行殿”，启民可汗亲自除草开道迎接；同年发丁男百余万修长城，西起榆林、东至紫河，“死者十五六”。

e.old: Emperor Yang tours the north · Great Wall repaired
e.note: On his northern tour Emperor Yang reached Yulin, where Yuwen Kai built a "Wind-Viewing Mobile Hall" that could hold several hundred people, and Qimin Qaghan cleared the grass with his own hands to open a road to welcome him. That year over a million able-bodied men were called up to repair the Great Wall, from Yulin in the west to the Zi River in the east, and "five or six in ten died".

items.old: 裴矩经营西域·置伊吾郡
items.note: 黄门侍郎裴矩在张掖主持互市，撰《西域图记》，记西域四十四国与三条通道；608 年薛世雄率军至伊吾，于汉旧伊吾城东筑新伊吾城，610 年置伊吾郡。

e.old: Pei Ju manages the Western Regions · Yiwu Commandery founded
e.note: Pei Ju, Vice Director of the Chancellery, ran the border markets at Zhangye and wrote the Illustrated Record of the Western Regions (Xiyu tuji), covering 44 states of the Western Regions and three routes. In 608 Xue Shixiong led an army to Yiwu and built New Yiwu City east of the old Han city of Yiwu; Yiwu Commandery was set up in 610.

items.note: 炀帝自西平穿越祁连山大斗拔谷至张掖，山路狭险，遭遇风雪，士卒冻死大半；六月在张掖接见高昌王麴伯雅、伊吾吐屯设等西域二十七国君长与使者，今人比之为“万国博览会”。

e.old: Emperor Yang tours the west · Dadouba Valley
e.note: Emperor Yang crossed the Qilian Mountains from Xiping by way of Dadouba Valley to Zhangye. The mountain road was narrow and dangerous, and in wind and snow more than half of the soldiers froze to death. In the 6th month at Zhangye he received the rulers and envoys of 27 states of the Western Regions, including Qu Boya, King of Gaochang, and the Tudun Shad of Yiwu, an event people today compare to a "World's Fair of All Nations".

items.note: 607、608 年朱宽两度出使流求，610 年陈稜、张镇州率东阳兵万余泛海击之，俘虏数千人而还。流求所指为今台湾或琉球，学界有争议。

e.note: Zhu Kuan went as envoy to Liuqiu twice, in 607 and 608. In 610 Chen Leng and Zhang Zhenzhou took over 10,000 troops from Dongyang across the sea to attack it, and came back with several thousand captives. Whether Liuqiu refers to present-day Taiwan or the Ryukyus is disputed among scholars.

items.mod: 山东章丘—邹平间长白山
items.note: 王薄自称“知世郎”，作《无向辽东浪死歌》，聚众长白山，拉开隋末民变序幕。同年窦建德、孙安祖在高鸡泊起事。

e.mod: Changbai Mountain between Zhangqiu and Zouping, Shandong
e.note: Wang Bo called himself the "Man Who Knows the World", wrote the song "Do Not Go to Liaodong to Die in Vain", and gathered followers on Changbai Mountain, raising the curtain on the popular risings of the late Sui. In the same year Dou Jiande and Sun Anzu rose at Gaoji Marsh.

items.note: 礼部尚书杨玄感在黎阳督运军粮，乘炀帝二征高句丽之机起兵，以李密为谋主，围攻东都；这是隋朝统治集团内部的第一次公开反叛。

e.note: Yang Xuangan, Minister of Rites, was overseeing grain transport for the army at Liyang when he seized the chance of Emperor Yang's second Goguryeo campaign to rise in arms. With Li Mi as his chief strategist he besieged the Eastern Capital. This was the first open rebellion from within the Sui ruling elite.

items.note: 炀帝不顾群臣劝阻第三次南下江都，留越王杨侗守东都、代王杨侑守大兴，此后再未北返。

e.note: Ignoring his ministers' objections, Emperor Yang went south to Jiangdu for the third time, leaving Yang Tong, Prince of Yue, to hold the Eastern Capital and Yang You, Prince of Dai, to hold Daxing. He never returned north.

items.note: 李密率精兵七千袭取兴洛仓，开仓任民取米，众至数十万，翟让推李密为主，称魏公，改元永平，檄文斥炀帝“罄南山之竹，书罪无穷”。

e.old: Li Mi takes the Xingluo Granary
e.note: Li Mi took the Xingluo Granary by surprise with 7,000 picked troops and opened it, letting the people take grain freely; his following swelled to several hundred thousand. Zhai Rang made Li Mi leader, and Li Mi styled himself Duke of Wei and changed the era name to Yongping. His proclamation denounced Emperor Yang: "Use up all the bamboo of the southern hills, and his crimes still could not all be written down".

items.note: 李世民与晋阳令刘文静、晋阳宫监裴寂谋划多时，劝李渊起事。五月李渊以“谋引突厥”为名斩副留守王威、高君雅，起兵；六月遣刘文静向始毕可汗称臣借马，七月誓师南下，打出“尊隋”旗号，传檄郡县。

e.note: Li Shimin had long plotted with Liu Wenjing, magistrate of Jinyang, and Pei Ji, superintendent of the Jinyang Palace, and urged Li Yuan to rise. In the 5th month, on the charge of "plotting to bring in the Turks", Li Yuan executed the deputy custodians Wang Wei and Gao Junya and rose in arms. In the 6th month he sent Liu Wenjing to Shibi Qaghan to declare himself a subject and borrow horses, and in the 7th month he swore an oath before his army and marched south under the banner of "honoring Sui", sending proclamations to the commanderies and counties.

items.note: 李渊攻河东城不下，采纳李世民之议留兵围之，主力自龙门渡河入关；李建成据永丰仓守潼关，李世民经略渭北，平阳公主的“娘子军”与关中豪杰纷纷来会。

e.old: Crossing at Longmen · Yongfeng Granary taken
e.note: Unable to take Hedong City, Li Yuan accepted Li Shimin's proposal to leave troops besieging it, while the main army crossed the Yellow River at Longmen into Guanzhong. Li Jiancheng held the Yongfeng Granary and guarded Tong Pass, Li Shimin campaigned north of the Wei, and Princess Pingyang's "Women's Army" (niangzi jun) and the local strongmen of Guanzhong flocked to join them.

items.note: 炀帝欲迁都丹阳，随驾的关中骁果思归，司马德戡、宇文化及等发动兵变，炀帝被缢杀于江都宫，年五十。

e.note: Emperor Yang wanted to move the capital to Danyang, while the Xiaoguo guards from Guanzhong who had followed him longed to go home. Sima Dekan, Yuwen Huaji and others staged a mutiny, and Emperor Yang was strangled in the Jiangdu Palace, aged 50.

items.note: 恭帝杨侑禅位，李渊在太极殿即皇帝位，国号唐，改元武德，立李建成为太子，封李世民为秦王、李元吉为齐王。

e.note: Emperor Gong, Yang You, abdicated, and Li Yuan took the imperial throne in the Taiji Hall. He named the dynasty Tang and changed the era name to Wude, made Li Jiancheng crown prince, and enfeoffed Li Shimin as Prince of Qin and Li Yuanji as Prince of Qi.

items.note: 李密邙山兵败后率二万人入关降唐，被授光禄卿，郁郁不得志；年底借口招抚旧部东出叛唐，在熊耳山被唐将盛彦师伏兵所杀，年三十七。

e.old: Li Mi submits to Tang and is killed
e.note: After his defeat at Mount Mang, Li Mi entered Guanzhong with 20,000 men and submitted to Tang. Made Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, he was frustrated and unfulfilled. At the end of the year he went east on the pretext of rallying his old followers and rebelled against Tang, but was killed in an ambush laid by the Tang general Sheng Yanshi in the Xiong'er Mountains, aged 37.

items.note: 王世充逼皇泰主杨侗禅位，即帝位，国号郑，改元开明；不久将杨侗杀害（饮鸩未绝，以帛缢杀），隋朝最后一位皇帝至此身死国灭。

e.note: Wang Shichong forced the Huangtai emperor, Yang Tong, to abdicate and took the throne himself, naming his state Zheng and changing the era name to Kaiming. Soon afterwards he had Yang Tong killed (the poison did not finish him, and he was strangled with silk); with that the last emperor of Sui was dead and his state destroyed.

items.note: 唐遣安兴贵入凉，与其弟安修仁（皆为凉州粟特胡人）联络诸胡起兵，围李轨于武威，执之送长安，河西五郡归唐。

e.note: Tang sent An Xinggui into Liang, where he and his younger brother An Xiuren (both Sogdians of Liangzhou) rallied the Hu peoples to rise. They besieged Li Gui at Wuwei, seized him and sent him to Chang'an, and the five commanderies of Hexi came over to Tang.

items.note: 杜伏威遣使降唐，拜东南道行台尚书令、淮南安抚大使，封楚王，后进封吴王，赐姓李，江淮名义上归入唐朝版图。

e.note: Du Fuwei sent envoys to submit to Tang and was appointed Director of the Southeast Branch Department and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, and enfeoffed as Prince of Chu; he was later raised to Prince of Wu and granted the imperial surname Li. Jianghuai thus nominally came within Tang territory.

items.note: 李世民围洛阳时，少林寺僧志操、昙宗等十三人擒获王世充之侄王仁则，以轘辕州城归唐；李世民赐书嘉奖，即“十三棍僧救唐王”故事的史实原型。

e.note: While Li Shimin was besieging Luoyang, 13 monks of the Shaolin Monastery, including Zhicao and Tanzong, captured Wang Shichong's nephew Wang Renze and handed the city of Huanyuan Zhou over to Tang. Li Shimin sent them a letter of commendation. This is the historical basis of the story of the "Thirteen Staff-Wielding Monks Who Saved the Prince of Tang".

items.note: 窦建德死后，旧部范愿、高雅贤等不愿入唐，推刘黑闼为主，在漳南起兵为窦建德复仇，半年间尽复夏国故地。

e.note: After Dou Jiande's death his former officers Fan Yuan, Gao Yaxian and others, unwilling to go over to Tang, made Liu Heita their leader and rose at Zhangnan to avenge Dou Jiande. Within half a year they had recovered all the former territory of Xia.

items.note: 废隋五铢，铸“开元通宝”，钱文由欧阳询书写，每十文重一两，开创以“文”为单位、以“宝”为钱名的通宝钱制，沿用至清末。

e.note: The Sui wuzhu coin was abolished and the "Kaiyuan tongbao" was cast, its inscription written by Ouyang Xun; ten coins weighed one liang. It began the tongbao coinage system, with the wen as the unit and "bao" in the coin's name, which remained in use until the end of the Qing.

items.note: 李世民平定洛阳后被加号天策上将，开天策府，又设文学馆，延揽杜如晦、房玄龄、虞世南、孔颖达等“十八学士”。

e.old: Supreme Commander of Heaven's Strategy · Academy of Literature
e.note: After pacifying Luoyang Li Shimin was given the additional title Supreme Commander of Heaven's Strategy and opened the Office of Heaven's Strategy. He also set up the Academy of Literature, recruiting the "Eighteen Scholars", including Du Ruhui, Fang Xuanling, Yu Shinan and Kong Yingda.

items.note: 辅公祏诈称杜伏威来信，起兵反唐，称帝国号宋；唐以李孝恭为元帅、李靖为副，分兵四路讨之。

e.note: Falsely claiming a letter from Du Fuwei, Fu Gongshi rose against Tang and proclaimed himself emperor of a state called Song. Tang sent Li Xiaogong as commander-in-chief, with Li Jing as his deputy, to attack him along four routes.

items.note: 颁行武德律、令，同时推行均田制与租庸调法：丁男受田一顷，岁输粟二石、绢二丈、绵三两，役二十日，不役者纳庸。

e.note: The Wude Code and Statutes were promulgated, together with the equal-field system and the zu-yong-diao taxes (grain, labor and cloth): each adult man received one qing of land and each year paid 2 shi of grain, 2 zhang of silk and 3 liang of silk floss and owed 20 days of labor service; those not called up paid yong instead.

items.note: 六月初四，秦王李世民率长孙无忌、尉迟敬德等伏兵于玄武门，李建成、李元吉入朝时遇伏，李世民亲手射杀李建成，尉迟敬德射杀李元吉。三日后李世民立为太子，八月即位。

e.mod: north gate of the Taiji Palace, Xi'an, Shaanxi
e.note: On the 4th day of the 6th month Li Shimin, Prince of Qin, laid an ambush at the Xuanwu Gate with Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde and others. Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji ran into it on their way to court; Li Shimin shot Li Jiancheng dead with his own hand, and Yuchi Jingde shot Li Yuanji. Three days later Li Shimin was made crown prince, and in the 8th month he took the throne.

items.note: 颉利、突利率十余万骑至渭水便桥北，太宗亲率高士廉、房玄龄等六骑至渭水边与颉利隔水相语，随后大军继至，颉利请和；八月三十日刑白马盟于便桥之上，突厥退兵。太宗视为“渭水之耻”，立志雪耻。

e.mod: Bian Bridge over the Wei, Xianyang, Shaanxi
e.note: Illig and Tuli came with over 100,000 horsemen to the north end of the Bian Bridge over the Wei. Taizong rode out with Gao Shilian, Fang Xuanling and others, six horsemen in all, to the bank of the Wei and spoke with Illig across the water; then the main army came up behind him, and Illig asked for peace. On the 30th day of the 8th month they sacrificed a white horse and swore a covenant on the Bian Bridge, and the Turks withdrew. Taizong regarded it as "the humiliation of the Wei River" and resolved to wipe it out.

items.note: 贞观元年并省州县，依山川形便分天下为关内、河南、河东、河北、山南、陇右、淮南、江南、剑南、岭南十道，作为监察区。

e.old: The realm divided into ten circuits
e.note: In Zhenguan 1 prefectures and counties were merged or abolished, and the realm was divided along the natural lines of mountains and rivers into ten circuits—Guannei, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Shannan, Longyou, Huainan, Jiangnan, Jiannan and Lingnan—as supervisory regions.

items.note: 玄奘私自出长安西行求法，在瓜州偷渡玉门关，独行莫贺延碛四夜五日几乎渴死，至伊吾、高昌，经西突厥、昭武诸国入天竺，在那烂陀寺从戒贤学法，645 年正月回到长安。

e.note: Xuanzang left Chang'an without permission to travel west in search of the Buddhist teachings. At Guazhou he slipped secretly past Yumen Pass, and crossing the Moheyan Desert alone he almost died of thirst over four nights and five days. He reached Yiwu and Gaochang, passed through the lands of the Western Turks and the Sogdian states (Zhaowu) into India, and studied under Silabhadra at Nalanda Monastery. He returned to Chang'an in the 1st month of 645.

items.note: 东突厥灭亡后，西北诸蕃君长诣阙，请太宗上尊号为“天可汗”，太宗曰“我为大唐天子，又下行可汗事乎？”群臣及四夷皆称万岁。此后对西北诸族的玺书皆称“天可汗”。

e.note: After the fall of the Eastern Turkic Qaghanate, the rulers of the northwestern peoples came to the court and asked Taizong to take the honorific title "Heavenly Qaghan". Taizong said, "I am the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang; shall I also stoop to the business of a qaghan?" The officials and the peoples of the four quarters all cried "Ten thousand years!" From then on, sealed edicts to the northwestern peoples all used the title "Heavenly Qaghan".

items.note: 平高昌后于交河城置安西都护府，以乔师望为都护，留兵镇守，这是唐朝在西域设立的第一个都护府。

e.note: After the conquest of Gaochang the Anxi Protectorate was set up at Jiaohe City, with Qiao Shiwang as protector-general and troops left to garrison it. It was the first protectorate Tang set up in the Western Regions.

items.note: 太宗以宗室女文成公主嫁吐蕃赞普松赞干布，江夏王李道宗护送，松赞干布亲至柏海（今鄂陵湖、扎陵湖）迎接。随行带去经史、医药、工匠与蔬菜种子。

e.note: Taizong married Princess Wencheng, a woman of the imperial clan, to the Tibetan tsenpo Songtsen Gampo, with Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, as her escort. Songtsen Gampo came in person to Baihai (today's Ngoring Lake and Gyaring Lake) to meet her. She brought with her classics and histories, medicines, craftsmen and vegetable seeds.

items.note: 太宗命阎立本在凌烟阁绘长孙无忌、李孝恭、杜如晦、魏征、房玄龄、尉迟敬德、李靖、李勣、秦叔宝等二十四位功臣画像。

e.old: Twenty-Four Meritorious Ministers of the Lingyan Pavilion
e.note: Taizong had Yan Liben paint portraits of 24 meritorious ministers in the Lingyan Pavilion, including Zhangsun Wuji, Li Xiaogong, Du Ruhui, Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, Yuchi Jingde, Li Jing, Li Ji and Qin Shubao.

items.note: 太宗至灵州，铁勒回纥、仆骨、同罗等十一部遣使请置唐官，尊太宗为天可汗；次年在回纥以南、突厥以北开参天可汗道，置邮驿六十八所，以通贡使。

e.note: When Taizong came to Lingzhou, 11 Tiele tribes, including the Huihe (Uyghurs), Pugu and Tongluo, sent envoys asking for Tang officials to be appointed over them and honored Taizong as Heavenly Qaghan. The next year the Road to the Heavenly Qaghan was opened south of the Huihe and north of the Turks, with 68 post stations to serve tribute envoys.

items.note: 以回纥部为瀚海都督府、仆骨为金微都督府、多滥葛为燕然都督府等六府七州，以各部酋长为都督、刺史，置燕然都护府于故单于台统之。

e.note: The Huihe (Uyghurs) were made the Hanhai Area Command, the Pugu the Jinwei Area Command, the Duolange the Yanran Area Command, and so on—six area commands and seven prefectures in all—with the chief of each tribe as area commander or prefect; the Yanran Protectorate was set up at the old Chanyu Terrace to govern them.

items.note: 契丹大贺氏首领窟哥、奚首领可度者率部内附，唐以契丹地置松漠都督府、奚地置饶乐都督府，皆隶营州都督府。

e.mod: around Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia
e.note: Kuge, chief of the Dahe clan of the Khitan, and Keduzhe, chief of the Xi, brought their peoples to submit to the empire. Tang set up the Songmo Area Command on Khitan land and the Raole Area Command on Xi land, both under the Yingzhou Area Command.

items.note: 王玄策出使天竺，适逢戒日王死、阿罗那顺篡位，使团被劫。王玄策逃至吐蕃，借吐蕃精兵一千二百、泥婆罗骑兵七千，大破中天竺军于茶镈和罗城，擒阿罗那顺献于长安。

e.note: Wang Xuance went as envoy to India just as Harsha died and Arunasva usurped the throne, and his mission was plundered. Wang Xuance escaped to Tibet and borrowed 1,200 picked Tibetan troops and 7,000 Nepalese cavalry; he crushed the army of Central India at Tirabhukti and captured Arunasva, whom he presented at Chang'an.

items.mod: 陕西西安长安区终南山
items.note: 太宗在终南山翠微宫病逝，年五十二（一说五十三），葬昭陵；太子李治即位于太极殿，是为高宗，长孙无忌、褚遂良受遗诏辅政。

e.old: Taizong dies at the Cuiwei Palace
e.mod: Zhongnan Mountains, Chang'an District, Xi'an, Shaanxi
e.note: Taizong died of illness at the Cuiwei Palace in the Zhongnan Mountains, aged 52 (or 53), and was buried at the Zhao Mausoleum. The crown prince Li Zhi took the throne in the Taiji Hall as Emperor Gaozong, and Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang received the testamentary edict to assist him in government.

items.note: 波斯王伊嗣俟三世被阿拉伯军追击，在木鹿被磨坊主所杀，萨珊王朝灭亡。其子卑路斯东奔吐火罗，屡次向唐求援。

e.note: Pursued by Arab armies, the Persian king Yazdegerd III was killed by a miller at Merv, and the Sasanian dynasty fell. His son Peroz fled east to Tokharistan and repeatedly asked Tang for help.

items.note: 长孙无忌等奉诏为《永徽律》作疏，653 年颁行，即今存的《唐律疏议》，为东亚各国法典的范本。

e.note: By imperial order Zhangsun Wuji and others wrote a commentary on the Yonghui Code (Yonghui lü). Promulgated in 653, it survives today as the Tang Code with Commentary (Tanglü shuyi) and served as the model for the law codes of the East Asian states.

items.note: 高宗不顾长孙无忌、褚遂良反对，废王皇后，立昭仪武氏为皇后；660 年后高宗风疾，武后渐参政事，号称“二圣”。

e.note: Over the objections of Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang, Gaozong deposed Empress Wang and made the Lady of Bright Deportment Wu his empress. After 660, when Gaozong suffered from a "wind" ailment, Empress Wu gradually took part in government, and the two were called the "Two Sages".

items.note: 高宗下诏以洛阳宫为东都，此后高宗、武后长期驻洛阳，政治重心逐渐东移。

e.note: Gaozong issued an edict making the Luoyang Palace the Eastern Capital. From then on Gaozong and Empress Wu spent long periods in Luoyang, and the political center of gravity gradually shifted east.

items.note: 平阿史那贺鲁后，安西都护府复移治龟兹，升为大都护府，以杨胄为都护，复置四镇。

e.note: After Ashina Helu was put down, the seat of the Anxi Protectorate was moved back to Kucha and it was raised to a grand protectorate, with Yang Zhou as protector-general; the Four Garrisons were re-established.

items.note: 陇州南由令王名远出使吐火罗诸国，奏请于于阗以西、波斯以东十六国置都督府，以阿缓城为月氏都督府、以疾陵城为波斯都督府等，凡都督府十六、州七十二、县一百一十，皆隶安西都护府，并立碑于吐火罗。

e.old: Sixteen area commands set up in the Western Regions
e.note: Wang Mingyuan, magistrate of Nanyou in Longzhou, went as envoy to the states of Tokharistan and memorialized asking that area commands be set up in 16 states west of Khotan and east of Persia. Warwaliz became the Yuezhi Area Command, Zaranj the Persian Area Command, and so on: 16 area commands, 72 prefectures and 110 counties in all, all under the Anxi Protectorate. A stele was also erected in Tokharistan.

items.note: 唐以新罗为鸡林州大都督府，以新罗王金法敏为大都督。

e.note: Tang made Silla the Gyerim Grand Area Command, with the Silla king Kim Beop-min as grand area commander.

items.note: 吐谷浑大臣素和贵叛逃吐蕃，尽言虚实；吐蕃大相禄东赞发兵攻破吐谷浑，诺曷钵与弘化公主率数千帐奔凉州，吐蕃尽有青海之地，唐蕃从此直接对峙。

e.note: The Tuyuhun minister Suhe Gui defected to Tibet and revealed all the Tuyuhun's strengths and weaknesses. The Tibetan chief minister Gar Tongtsen sent troops and crushed the Tuyuhun; Nuohebo and Princess Honghua fled to Liangzhou with several thousand tents, Tibet took all the land of Qinghai, and from then on Tang and Tibet faced each other directly.

items.note: 于弄栋川置姚州都督府，管辖洱海周边的羁縻州县，与吐蕃争夺南中。

e.note: The Yaozhou Area Command was set up at Nongdongchuan to govern the loose-rein prefectures and counties around Erhai Lake and to contest Nanzhong with Tibet.

items.note: 高宗率百官及突厥、于阗、波斯、天竺、倭、新罗、百济、高句丽等国使者封禅泰山，武后以亚献身份参与禅社首山之礼，开女性参与封禅之先例。

e.old: Feng and shan sacrifices at Mount Tai
e.note: Gaozong, with the officials and envoys from the Turks, Khotan, Persia, India, Wa, Silla, Baekje, Goguryeo and other states, performed the feng and shan sacrifices at Mount Tai. Empress Wu took part in the shan rite on Mount Sheshou as second offerant, setting a precedent for women taking part in the feng and shan.

items.note: 泉盖苏文死后长子泉男生继任莫离支，出巡时被二弟泉男建、泉男产夺权，泉男生据国内城求救于唐，唐由此出兵。

e.note: After the death of Yeon Gaesomun his eldest son Yeon Namsaeng succeeded him as Mangniji, but while he was away on a tour of inspection his two younger brothers Yeon Namgeon and Yeon Namsan seized power. Yeon Namsaeng held Gungnae Fortress and asked Tang for help, and so Tang sent troops.

items.note: 于平壤置安东都护府，以薛仁贵为检校安东都护，率兵二万镇守，分高句丽地为九都督府、四十二州、百县。

e.note: The Andong Protectorate was set up at Pyongyang, with Xue Rengui as acting protector-general of Andong, holding it with 20,000 troops. The lands of Goguryeo were divided into nine area commands, 42 prefectures and 100 counties.

items.note: 吐蕃陷西域十八州，又与于阗袭龟兹拨换城，唐罢龟兹、于阗、焉耆、疏勒四镇。

e.old: Tibet takes eighteen prefectures of the Western Regions
e.note: Tibet took eighteen prefectures of the Western Regions and, together with Khotan, attacked Bohuan City in Kucha; Tang abolished the Four Garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Karasahr and Kashgar.

items.note: 高句丽遗民剑牟岑起兵，立宝藏王外孙安舜为王，后投新罗；唐遣高侃讨之，至 673 年平定。

e.note: Geom Mojam, of the Goguryeo remnant population, rose in arms and made An Seung, the son of King Bojang's daughter, king; An Seung later went over to Silla. Tang sent Gao Kan against them, and the rising was put down by 673.

items.note: 高宗称天皇、武后称天后，改元上元；武后建言十二事，二圣临朝。

e.old: Gaozong takes the title Heavenly Emperor
e.note: Gaozong took the title Heavenly Emperor and Empress Wu the title Heavenly Empress, and the era name was changed to Shangyuan. Empress Wu put forward twelve proposals, and the Two Sages held court together.

items.note: 以鄯善故城典合城为石城镇、且末城为播仙镇，隶沙州，扼西域南道。

e.note: Dianhe City, the old city of Shanshan, was made Shicheng Garrison and Qiemo City was made Boxian Garrison; both were placed under Shazhou and controlled the southern route of the Western Regions.

items.note: 安东都护府自平壤移辽东故城，次年再移新城；熊津都督府移建安故城。唐从此退出朝鲜半岛南部。

e.note: The Andong Protectorate moved from Pyongyang to the old Yodong Fortress, and the next year moved again to Sinseong; the Ungjin Area Command moved to the old Geonan Fortress. With this Tang withdrew from the southern part of the Korean Peninsula.

items.mod: 吉尔吉斯斯坦托克马克东
items.note: 裴行俭以册送波斯王子泥涅师为名，至西州召四镇诸蕃子弟随行校猎，倍道西进，突至都支牙帐擒之，李遮匐亦降；王方翼留筑碎叶城，四面十二门。

e.note: On the pretext of investing the Persian prince Narseh and escorting him home, Pei Xingjian went to Xizhou, where he summoned the young men of the peoples of the Four Garrisons to join him on a hunt. Then, marching west at double speed, he burst upon Ashina Duzhi's royal camp and captured him, and Li Zhefu also surrendered. Wang Fangyi stayed behind to build Suyab, with twelve gates on its four sides.
e.yt: 7th month, 679 (9th month in the annals of both Tang histories)

items.note: 单于都护府所领突厥阿史德温傅、奉职二部叛，立阿史那泥熟匐为可汗，二十四州酋长皆叛应之。

e.note: Two Turkic tribes under the Chanyu Protectorate, those of Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi, rebelled and set up Ashina Nishufu as qaghan, and the chiefs of 24 prefectures all rebelled in support.

items.note: 生羌为吐蕃向导，陷安戎城，吐蕃据之以逼西川；西洱诸蛮皆降于吐蕃，吐蕃“地方万余里”。

e.note: With the unsubjugated Qiang as its guides, Tibet took Anrong City and held it to threaten Xichuan. The Xi'er tribes all submitted to Tibet, whose territory now covered "over 10,000 li square".

items.note: 颉利族人阿史那骨咄禄招集亡散，据黑沙城，暾欲谷为谋主，自立为可汗，后突厥复兴。

e.note: Ashina Qutlugh, a kinsman of Illig, gathered the scattered Turks and held Heisha City. With Tonyukuk as his chief strategist he proclaimed himself qaghan, and the Turkic state was revived as the Second Turkic Qaghanate.

items.note: 高宗 683 年十二月崩于洛阳；684 年武后废中宗、立睿宗，临朝称制，九月改东都为神都，旗帜改从金色。

e.old: Eastern Capital renamed the Divine Capital
e.note: Gaozong died at Luoyang in the 12th month of 683. In 684 Empress Wu deposed Zhongzong, set up Ruizong and ruled from the court in her own name; in the 9th month the Eastern Capital was renamed the Divine Capital, and the banners were changed to gold.

items.note: 后突厥据漠北，唐于同城侨置安北都护府；垂拱间回纥、契苾、思结、浑四部南迁甘、凉之间。

e.old: Anbei Protectorate temporarily seated at Tongcheng
e.note: With the Second Turks holding the lands north of the Gobi, Tang set up the Anbei Protectorate temporarily at Tongcheng. In the Chuigong era four tribes—the Huihe (Uyghurs), Qibi, Sijie and Hun—moved south to the area between Ganzhou and Liangzhou.

items.note: 唐拔弃安西四镇，吐蕃乘虚而入；陈子昂上疏言“弃龟兹，放疏勒”之害。年份史无明文。

e.note: Tang withdrew from and abandoned the Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Tibet moved into the vacuum; Chen Zi'ang sent up a memorial on the harm of "abandoning Kucha and letting Kashgar go". The sources do not record the year.

items.note: 武则天称圣神皇帝，改国号周，改元天授，以神都为都，立武氏七庙；691 年旗帜尚赤。705 年复唐。

e.note: Wu Zetian took the title Sage and Divine Emperor, changed the name of the dynasty to Zhou and the era name to Tianshou, made the Divine Capital her capital and set up seven ancestral temples for the Wu family; in 691 red was adopted for the banners. Tang was restored in 705.

items.note: 骨咄禄死，其弟默啜自立为可汗，后突厥国势达于顶点。

e.note: Qutlugh died, and his younger brother Qapaghan made himself qaghan; the power of the Second Turkic Qaghanate reached its height.

items.note: 契丹松漠都督李尽忠与归诚州刺史孙万荣因营州都督赵文翙侵侮，杀文翙，据营州反，李尽忠自号无上可汗。

e.note: Provoked by the abuses and insults of Zhao Wenhui, area commander of Yingzhou, Li Jinzhong, the Khitan area commander of Songmo, and Sun Wanrong, prefect of Guicheng Zhou, killed Zhao Wenhui and rose in revolt, holding Yingzhou; Li Jinzhong styled himself Wushang Qaghan.

items.note: 武则天以武延秀聘默啜女，默啜以“我女拟嫁李氏，安用武氏儿”为辞，发兵南下，八月陷定州，九月围赵州，退兵时尽杀所掠赵、定等州男女万余人，自五回道去（《旧唐书·突厥传》作掠八九万人）。

e.note: Wu Zetian sent Wu Yanxiu to marry Qapaghan's daughter. Using the words "My daughter was meant to marry a Li; what use is a son of the Wu clan?" as his pretext, Qapaghan sent his army south; in the 8th month he took Dingzhou and in the 9th month besieged Zhaozhou. As he withdrew he killed all the more than 10,000 men and women he had seized in Zhaozhou, Dingzhou and other prefectures, and left by the Wuhui Road (the "Turks" chapter of the Old Book of Tang says he carried off 80,000 or 90,000 people).

items.note: 大祚荣率粟末靺鞨与高句丽遗民东走，据东牟山筑城以居，自号震国王。

e.note: Dae Joyeong led the Sumo Mohe and the Goguryeo remnant population east; he held Mount Dongmou, built a walled town there to live in, and styled himself King of Jin.

items.note: 赞普器弩悉弄设计诛噶尔家族，论钦陵兵败自杀，其弟赞婆与钦陵子论弓仁率众降唐。

e.note: The tsenpo Tridu Songtsen plotted to destroy the Gar clan. Gar Trinring was defeated and killed himself, and his younger brother Gar Tsenba and his son Lun Gongren went over to Tang with their followers.

items.mod: 新疆吉木萨尔北庭故城
items.note: 分安西都护府天山以北之地，于庭州置北庭都护府，统西突厥故地诸羁縻府州。

e.note: The lands of the Anxi Protectorate north of the Tian Shan were split off, and the Beiting Protectorate was set up at Tingzhou to govern the loose-rein area commands and prefectures in the former lands of the Western Turks.

items.mod: 吉尔吉斯斯坦托克马克
items.note: 突骑施乌质勒攻陷碎叶，徙牙帐于此，西突厥十姓多归之。

e.note: Üch Elig of the Türgesh took Suyab and moved his royal camp there, and most of the Ten Tribes of the Western Turks went over to him.

items.note: 张柬之、崔玄暐、桓彦范等率羽林军诛张易之、张昌宗，迫武则天传位于太子李显（中宗），二月复国号唐。

e.note: Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Huan Yanfan and others led the Yulin Guards to kill Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong and forced Wu Zetian to pass the throne to the crown prince Li Xian (Zhongzong); in the 2nd month the dynasty's name was changed back to Tang.

items.note: 朔方道大总管张仁愿乘默啜西击突骑施，于河北筑东、中、西三受降城，相距各四百余里，置烽候千八百所，自此突厥不敢度山畋牧。

e.old: Building of the Three Shouxiang Cities
e.note: Taking advantage of Qapaghan's campaign west against the Türgesh, Zhang Renyuan, commander-in-chief of the Shuofang Route, built the Eastern, Central and Western Shouxiang Cities north of the Yellow River, each over 400 li from the next, and set up 1,800 beacon posts. From then on the Turks did not dare to cross the mountains to hunt and graze.

items.note: 中宗暴崩，韦后临朝；临淄王李隆基与太平公主发兵诛韦后、安乐公主，睿宗复位。

e.note: Zhongzong died suddenly, and Empress Wei took control of the court. Li Longji, Prince of Linzi, and Princess Taiping raised troops and killed Empress Wei and Princess Anle, and Ruizong was restored to the throne.

items.note: 以贺拔延嗣为凉州都督、河西节度使，统凉、甘、肃、伊、瓜、沙、西七州（《新唐书·方镇表》系于景云元年；《唐会要》《通典》作景云二年四月，并称此始有节度之号；《通鉴》则谓节度使之名始于 710 年十月幽州薛讷）。

e.note: Heba Yansi was made area commander of Liangzhou and military governor of Hexi, in charge of seven prefectures: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou, Guazhou, Shazhou and Xizhou (the New Book of Tang's table of military governors dates it to Jingyun 1; the Tang huiyao and the Tongdian give the 4th month of Jingyun 2, and both say that the title of military governor began here; the Zizhi tongjian, however, says that the title began with Xue Ne at Youzhou in the 10th month of 710).

items.note: 712 年八月睿宗传位，玄宗即位；713 年七月玄宗诛太平公主一党，十二月改元开元。

e.note: In the 8th month of 712 Ruizong abdicated and Xuanzong took the throne. In the 7th month of 713 Xuanzong destroyed Princess Taiping's faction, and in the 12th month the era name was changed to Kaiyuan.

items.note: 唐遣崔訢册大祚荣为左骁卫大将军、渤海郡王，以其地为忽汗州，加授忽汗州都督，自是去靺鞨号，专称渤海。

e.note: Tang sent Cui Xin to invest Dae Joyeong as Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard and Commandery Prince of Bohai, made his land Huhan Zhou and gave him the further title of area commander of Huhan Zhou. From then on the state dropped the name Mohe and called itself simply Balhae.

items.note: 716 年契丹李失活、奚李大酺率众内附，复置松漠、饶乐都督府；717 年复于柳城置营州都督府。

e.note: In 716 Li Shihuo of the Khitan and Li Dapu of the Xi brought their peoples over to Tang, and the Songmo and Raole Area Commands were re-established; in 717 the Yingzhou Area Command was set up again at Liucheng.

items.note: 玄宗东封泰山，突厥、大食、日本、新罗等诸国使者扈从。

e.old: Feng and shan sacrifices at Mount Tai
e.note: Xuanzong went east to perform the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, attended by envoys from the Turks, the Arab Caliphate, Japan, Silla and other states.

items.note: 以黑水靺鞨地置黑水都督府，置长史监之；渤海王大武艺以为腹背受敌，发兵讨黑水，弟大门艺谏而奔唐。

e.note: The Heishui Area Command was set up on the lands of the Heishui Mohe, with an aide appointed to supervise it. Dae Muye, King of Balhae, believing he would be attacked from front and rear, sent troops against the Heishui; his younger brother Dae Munye remonstrated and then fled to Tang.

items.note: 分天下为京畿、关内、都畿、河南、河东、河北、陇右、山南东、山南西、剑南、淮南、江南东、江南西、黔中、岭南十五道，各置采访处置使。

e.old: The realm divided into fifteen circuits
e.note: The realm was divided into fifteen circuits—the Capital District, Guannei, the Eastern Capital District, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Longyou, Shannan East, Shannan West, Jiannan, Huainan, Jiangnan East, Jiangnan West, Qianzhong and Lingnan—each with a surveillance commissioner.

items.note: 唐蕃于赤岭（今日月山）定界立碑；先是吐蕃请互市于甘松岭，唐以甘松险阻不许，改于赤岭互市。738 年六月唐廷下令毁碑。
items.yt: 734 年六月（《唐会要》作 733 年九月）

e.note: Tang and Tibet fixed their boundary at Chiling (today's Riyue Mountain) and erected a stele there. Earlier Tibet had asked to open border markets at Gansong Pass; Tang refused because Gansong was too rugged, and the markets were held at Chiling instead. In the 6th month of 738 the Tang court ordered the stele destroyed.
e.yt: 6th month, 734 (9th month, 733 in the Tang huiyao)

items.note: 幽州节度使张守珪诱契丹衙官李过折，斩可突于及其王屈烈，传首东都；契丹、奚复归唐。

e.note: Zhang Shougui, military governor of Youzhou, induced the Khitan officer Li Guozhe to behead Ketuyu and the king Qulie, and the heads were sent to the Eastern Capital. The Khitan and the Xi returned to Tang allegiance.

items.note: 唐以浿江（大同江）以南之地正式赐新罗，承认新罗据有朝鲜半岛大同江以南。

e.old: Lands south of the Paegang granted to Silla
e.note: Tang formally granted Silla the land south of the Paegang (the Taedong River), recognizing Silla's possession of the Korean Peninsula south of the Taedong River.

items.note: 蒙舍诏皮罗阁在唐支持下兼并蒙巂、越析、浪穹、邆赕、施浪五诏，唐册封为云南王、赐名蒙归义，次年迁都太和城。

e.note: With Tang support Piluoge of the Mengshe zhao annexed the other five zhao—Mengxi, Yuexi, Langqiong, Dengtan and Shilang. Tang invested him as Prince of Yunnan and gave him the name Meng Guiyi, and the next year he moved his capital to Taihe City.

items.note: 改元天宝，于边境置安西、北庭、河西、朔方、河东、范阳、平卢、陇右、剑南九节度与岭南五府经略使，统兵四十九万；同年改州为郡、刺史为太守。

e.note: The era name was changed to Tianbao. On the frontiers nine military governors were set up—for Anxi, Beiting, Hexi, Shuofang, Hedong, Fanyang, Pinglu, Longyou and Jiannan—together with the pacification commissioner of the Five Commands of Lingnan, commanding 490,000 troops in all. The same year prefectures were renamed commanderies and prefects became governors.

items.note: 回纥骨力裴罗与葛逻禄攻杀拔悉密颉跌伊施可汗，自立为骨咄禄毗伽阙可汗，唐册为怀仁可汗，南居突厥故地，立牙帐于乌德鞬山。

e.note: Guli Peiluo of the Uyghurs, together with the Karluks, attacked and killed Xiedie Yishi Qaghan of the Basmyl and proclaimed himself Qutlugh Bilge Kül Qaghan; Tang invested him as Huairen Qaghan. He moved south to live in the former lands of the Turks and set up his royal camp at Ötüken.

items.note: 回纥怀仁可汗击杀后突厥白眉可汗，传首京师，后突厥亡，漠北尽为回纥所有。

e.old: Fall of the Second Turkic Qaghanate
e.note: Huairen Qaghan of the Uyghurs attacked and killed Baimei Qaghan of the Second Turks and sent his head to the capital. The Second Turkic Qaghanate fell, and all the lands north of the Gobi passed to the Uyghurs.

items.note: 安禄山欲以边功邀宠，屡侵契丹、奚；两蕃各杀和亲的静乐公主、宜芳公主叛唐，安禄山讨破之。

e.old: Khitan and Xi revolt against Tang
e.note: Seeking imperial favor through frontier exploits, An Lushan repeatedly attacked the Khitan and the Xi. The two peoples each killed the princess given to them in a marriage alliance—Princess Jingle and Princess Yifang—and rebelled against Tang; An Lushan attacked and defeated them.

items.note: 哥舒翰于青海湖中龙驹岛筑应龙城，又于青海上筑神威军，吐蕃不敢近青海。

e.note: Geshu Han built Yinglong City on Longju Island in Qinghai Lake and also built the Shenwei Jun by the lake, and Tibet did not dare come near Qinghai Lake.

items.mod: 吉尔吉斯斯坦托克马克
items.note: 北庭节度使王正见薄伐碎叶，城壁摧毁，邑居零落（杜环《经行记》）。

e.note: Wang Zhengjian, military governor of Beiting, attacked Suyab; its walls were destroyed and its dwellings left in ruins (per Du Huan's Jingxing ji).

items.note: 高仙芝以石国“无蕃臣礼”为名，伪与约和，引兵袭之，虏其王及部众献于长安，石国王被斩于阙下，王子逃奔诸胡，引大食兵来攻。

e.note: On the grounds that Chach "lacked the courtesy of a vassal", Gao Xianzhi pretended to make peace with it, then attacked it by surprise, captured its king and people and presented them at Chang'an. The king of Chach was beheaded before the palace gates; his son fled to the other Hu states and brought in troops of the Arab Caliphate to attack.

items.note: 阿布·穆斯林 747 年起兵呼罗珊，750 年阿拔斯王朝代倭马亚王朝，唐称黑衣大食（倭马亚为白衣大食）。

e.note: Abu Muslim rose in arms in Khorasan in 747, and in 750 the Abbasid dynasty replaced the Umayyad dynasty. Tang called the Abbasids the "Black-Robed Arabs" (and the Umayyads the "White-Robed Arabs").

items.note: 云南太守张虔陀侮辱南诏王阁罗凤，阁罗凤怒而发兵攻陷姚州（云南郡），杀张虔陀，取夷州三十二。

e.note: Zhang Qiantuo, governor of Yunnan Commandery, insulted Geluofeng, King of Nanzhao. In anger Geluofeng sent troops, took Yaozhou (Yunnan Commandery), killed Zhang Qiantuo and seized 32 tribal prefectures.

items.note: 吐蕃册阁罗凤为“赞普钟南国大诏”（赞普之弟），南诏改元赞普钟，北臣吐蕃（《南诏德化碑》）。

e.note: Tibet invested Geluofeng as "Tsenpo Zhong, Great Zhao of the Southern Kingdom" ("younger brother of the tsenpo"); Nanzhao changed its era name to Tsenpo Zhong and turned north to become a vassal of Tibet (per the Nanzhao Dehua Stele).

items.mod: 青海共和、同德一带（确址未定）
items.note: 以哥舒翰所收九曲之地置洮阳、浇河二郡及神策军、宛秀军，唐陇右西境推到黄河九曲。

e.mod: around Gonghe and Tongde, Qinghai (exact site uncertain)
e.note: Taoyang and Jiaohe Commanderies and the Shence Jun and Wanxiu Jun were set up in the Jiuqu lands taken by Geshu Han, and the western frontier of Tang Longyou was pushed out to the Jiuqu bend of the Yellow River.

items.note: 关中的南屏，隋唐人称南山、终南山，有子午、傥骆、褒斜、陈仓等谷道入汉中；649 年太宗崩于山中翠微宫。

e.note: The southern screen of Guanzhong, called the Southern Mountains (Nanshan) or the Zhongnan Mountains in Sui and Tang times; valley roads such as the Ziwu, Tangluo, Baoye and Chencang crossed them into Hanzhong. Emperor Taizong died at the Cuiwei Palace in these mountains in 649.

items.note: 汉中与巴蜀之间的屏障，米仓道、荔枝道翻越于此。

e.note: The barrier between Hanzhong and Ba and Shu, crossed by the Micang Road and the Lizhi Road.

items.note: 河东与河北的分界，有“太行八陉”沟通；隋末唐初李唐据河东、窦建德据河北，即隔此山相峙。

e.note: The divide between Hedong and Hebei, crossed by the "Eight Defiles of the Taihang". In the late Sui and early Tang the Li family's Tang held Hedong and Dou Jiande held Hebei, facing each other across these mountains.

items.note: 河东西部山地，西临黄河。

e.note: The uplands of western Hedong, bordered by the Yellow River on the west.

items.note: 河东蒲州之南，解县盐池在其北麓。

e.note: South of Puzhou in Hedong; the salt lake of Xie County lies at its northern foot.

items.note: 北岳。唐代祭祀北岳在曲阳（北岳庙），所祭为今河北阜平、唐县交界的大茂山。

e.note: The Northern Peak. In Tang times the sacrifices to the Northern Peak were made at Quyang (the Northern Peak Temple); the mountain worshipped was today's Mount Damao, on the border of Fuping and Tang County, Hebei.

items.note: 文殊菩萨道场，唐代佛教圣地。

e.note: The sacred seat of the bodhisattva Manjushri, a Buddhist holy place in Tang times.

items.note: 幽州北面屏障，居庸、古北、渝关诸关所在，隋唐防御突厥、奚、契丹皆倚此线。

e.note: The northern shield of Youzhou, where Juyong Pass, Gubeikou and Yu Pass stood; Sui and Tang defenses against the Turks, Xi and Khitan all relied on this line.

items.note: 漠南草原与河套之间的屏障；583 年隋破突厥于白道，630 年李靖、李勣袭破颉利可汗于阴山北麓。

e.note: The barrier between the steppe south of the Gobi and the Ordos Loop; in 583 Sui defeated the Turks at Baidao, and in 630 Li Jing and Li Ji routed Illig Qaghan in a surprise attack at the northern foot of the Yin Mountains.

items.note: 灵州西北屏障。

e.note: The northwestern shield of Lingzhou.

items.note: 关中与陇右之间的屏障，618 年薛举、薛仁杲与唐军在其东的浅水原两度决战。

e.note: The barrier between Guanzhong and Longyou; in 618 Xue Ju and Xue Rengao fought two decisive battles against the Tang army at Qianshuiyuan, to its east.

items.note: 河西走廊南侧，唐人亦称南山、雪山。

e.note: On the south side of the Hexi Corridor; Tang people also called it the Southern Mountains (Nanshan) or the Snow Mountains (Xueshan).

items.note: 西域南道与青海之间，吐谷浑由此控制鄯善、且末。

e.note: Between the southern route through the Western Regions and Qinghai; from here the Tuyuhun controlled Shanshan and Qiemo.

items.note: 于阗南山，产玉。

e.note: Khotan's southern mountains, a source of jade.

items.note: 唐称大积石山，黄河绕其而过。

e.note: Called the Great Jishi Mountains in Tang times; the Yellow River curves around them.

items.note: 唐蕃古道翻越此山入藏北（今名）。

e.note: The Tang–Tibet road crossed these mountains into northern Tibet (modern name).

items.note: 藏南谷地北缘（今名）。

e.note: The northern edge of the valleys of southern Tibet (modern name).

items.note: 吐蕃与天竺、泥婆罗之间的大雪山；648 年王玄策借吐蕃、泥婆罗兵翻越而下平定中天竺。

e.note: The great snowy range between Tibet on one side and India and Nepal on the other; in 648 Wang Xuance, with troops borrowed from Tibet and Nepal, crossed it and came down to subdue Central India.

items.note: 西域与河中、吐火罗的分界，玄奘西行、东归两次翻越；658 年以后，唐的羁縻府州远及葱岭以西。

e.note: The divide between the Western Regions and Transoxiana and Tokharistan; Xuanzang crossed it twice, going west and returning east. From 658 on, Tang loose-rein area commands and prefectures reached beyond the Pamirs.

items.note: 隋唐称天山、白山，东段又名折罗漫山；北为西突厥游牧之地，南为焉耆、龟兹等绿洲国家。

e.note: Called the Tian Shan or the White Mountains (Baishan) in Sui and Tang times, with the eastern section also known as the Zheluoman Mountains. To the north lay the grazing lands of the Western Turks, to the south oasis states such as Karasahr and Kucha.

items.note: 阿尔泰山，突厥起源于金山之阳；650 年唐将高侃在此擒车鼻可汗。

e.note: The Turks originated on the southern slopes of these mountains; in 650 the Tang general Gao Kan captured Chebi Qaghan here.

items.note: 杭爱山，漠北腹地；突厥、薛延陀牙帐所在的于都斤山（郁督军山）即其东段。

e.note: The Khangai Mountains, in the heart of the land north of the Gobi; Ötüken (Yudujun Mountain), where the Turkic and Xueyantuo royal camps stood, is their eastern section.

items.note: 室韦、契丹与漠北诸部之间（今名）。

e.note: Between the Shiwei and Khitan and the tribes north of the Gobi (modern name).

items.note: 长白山，唐称太白山、徒太山，靺鞨白山部居其北。

e.note: The Changbai Mountains, called Mount Taibai or Mount Tutai in Tang times; the White Mountain (Baishan) tribe of the Mohe lived to the north.

items.note: 辽西名山，隋唐东征高句丽时大军经其南麓。

e.note: A famous mountain range of Liaoxi; the Sui and Tang armies marching east against Goguryeo passed along its southern foot.

items.note: 东岳，666 年正月唐高宗与武后封禅于此。

e.note: The Eastern Peak; in the 1st month of 666 Emperor Gaozong of Tang and Empress Wu performed the feng and shan sacrifices here.

items.note: 西岳，潼关以西。

e.note: The Western Peak, west of Tong Pass.

items.note: 中岳，少林寺所在；621 年少林寺僧助李世民擒王仁则。

e.note: The Central Peak, site of the Shaolin Monastery; in 621 Shaolin monks helped Li Shimin capture Wang Renze.

items.note: 洛阳与南阳盆地之间。

e.note: Between Luoyang and the Nanyang Basin.

items.note: 淮南与江夏之间。

e.note: Between Huainan and Jiangxia.

items.note: 长江三峡所在。

e.note: Where the Three Gorges of the Yangtze lie.

items.note: 五溪蛮聚居之地。

e.note: Home of the Five Streams tribes.

items.note: 资水、沅水之间（今名）。

e.note: Between the Zi and Yuan rivers (modern name).

items.note: 越城、都庞、萌渚、骑田、大庾五岭，岭南与中原的分界。

e.note: The five ridges of Yuecheng, Dupang, Mengzhu, Qitian and Dayu, forming the divide between Lingnan and the Central Plains.

items.note: 湖南、江西之间（今名）。

e.note: Between Hunan and Jiangxi (modern name).

items.note: 福建与江西之间。

e.note: Between Fujian and Jiangxi.

items.note: 浙、闽之间的山隘。

e.note: A mountain pass between Zhejiang and Fujian.

items.note: 又称匡庐，九江郡南，东晋慧远在此创东林寺。

e.note: Also called Kuanglu; south of Jiujiang Commandery, where Huiyuan of the Eastern Jin founded the Donglin Temple.

items.note: 南岳。

e.note: The Southern Peak.

items.note: 松州所在，638 年吐蕃进攻松州，被唐将牛进达夜袭击退。

e.note: Site of Songzhou; in 638 Tibet attacked Songzhou and was driven back by a night raid under the Tang general Niu Jinda.

items.note: 成都平原西缘，与诸羌相接。

e.note: The western edge of the Chengdu Plain, bordering the Qiang tribes.

items.note: 川西高原东缘（今名）。

e.note: The eastern edge of the western Sichuan plateau (modern name).

items.note: 洱海西岸，洱海诸部居其下。

e.note: On the west shore of Erhai Lake, with the Erhai tribes living below it.

items.note: 洱海诸部东南（今名）。

e.note: Southeast of the Erhai tribes (modern name).

items.note: 玄奘称大雪山，吐火罗与天竺之间的屏障，梵衍那、迦毕试皆在其山中；661 年唐于其地设写凤、修鲜等都督府。

e.note: Xuanzang called it the Great Snow Mountains: the barrier between Tokharistan and India, with Bamiyan and Kapisa both in its mountains. In 661 Tang set up the Xiefeng, Xiuxian and other area commands there.

items.note: 河东中轴，晋阳、晋州、绛州皆临汾水。617 年李渊沿汾水南下，霍邑、龙门之役皆在其流域；619—620 年李世民与宋金刚在下游柏壁、上游雀鼠谷先后决战。

e.note: The central axis of Hedong: Jinyang, Jinzhou and Jiangzhou all stood on the Fen. In 617 Li Yuan marched south along the Fen, and the fighting at Huoyi and Longmen took place in its basin; in 619–620 Li Shimin fought decisive battles against Song Jingang, first at Baibi on its lower course and then at Queshu Valley on its upper course.

items.note: 长江上游。

e.note: The upper reaches of the Yangtze.

items.note: 唐称泸水，即金沙江，隋唐时巂州与南中诸蛮的界水。

e.note: Called the Lu River in Tang times; it is the Jinsha River. In Sui and Tang times it was the boundary between Xizhou and the tribes of Nanzhong.

items.note: 大江。581—589 年隋与陈以长江为界；589 年贺若弼自广陵、韩擒虎自横江夜渡袭采石，灭陈。621 年李孝恭、李靖乘秋水自夔州顺流而下，直抵江陵。

e.note: The Great River (Dajiang). In 581–589 the Sui and Chen used the Yangtze as their border; in 589 Heruo Bi crossed it from Guangling, and Han Qinhu crossed by night from Hengjiang to take Caishi, destroying Chen. In 621 Li Xiaogong and Li Jing rode the autumn floods downstream from Kuizhou straight to Jiangling.

items.note: 沔水，襄阳为汉水中游重镇；隋末王世充之侄王弘烈据襄阳，621 年降唐。

e.note: Also called the Mian River; Xiangyang was the key city on its middle course. In the late Sui Wang Shichong's nephew Wang Honglie held Xiangyang, and he surrendered to Tang in 621.

items.note: 色楞格河，回纥、仆骨等铁勒部落游牧之地，647 年唐于其地设瀚海等都督府。
