e.note: Grazing land of Tiele tribes such as the Huihe and Pugu; in 647 Tang set up the Hanhai and other area commands there.

items.note: 交州的母亲河，交州临其右岸。

e.note: The mother river of Jiaozhou, which stood on its right bank.

items.note: 川西与诸羌部落的天然分界。

e.note: A natural boundary between western Sichuan and the Qiang tribes.

items.note: 契丹发源地，大贺氏部落联盟居其流域，648 年唐置松漠都督府。

e.note: Birthplace of the Khitan; the Dahe tribal confederation lived in its basin, and in 648 Tang set up the Songmo Area Command there.

items.note: 松花江，粟末靺鞨居其流域，后来建立渤海国。

e.note: The Songhua River, along which the Sumo Mohe lived; they later founded the state of Balhae.

items.note: 成都平原的水源，都江堰在其上。

e.note: The water source of the Chengdu Plain, with the Dujiangyan irrigation works on it.

items.note: 澜沧江，洱海诸部西境。

e.note: The western border of the Erhai tribes.

items.note: 代北与幽州之间的大河，马邑、恒安一带，下游称卢沟水。

e.note: The great river between Daibei and Youzhou, flowing through the Mayi and Heng'an area; its lower course was called the Lugou River.

items.note: 雅鲁藏布江，吐蕃发祥的雅隆河谷即在其南岸，逻些在其支流吉曲河畔。

e.note: The Yarlung Tsangpo. The Yarlung Valley, cradle of Tibet, lies on its south bank, and Rasa stands beside its tributary the Kyichu.

items.note: 唐称涪陵江、黔江。

e.note: Called the Fuling River or the Qian River in Tang times.

items.note: 淮水。隋唐时淮河经泗州、楚州独流入海；通济渠在盱眙北入淮，山阳渎在山阳接淮，是南北漕运的枢纽。

e.note: In Sui and Tang times the Huai flowed to the sea by its own channel past Sizhou and Chuzhou. The Tongji Canal entered the Huai north of Xuyi and the Shanyang Canal joined it at Shanyang, making it the hub of north–south grain transport.

items.note: 建溪、富屯溪汇合后经福州入海。

e.note: Formed where the Jian and Futun streams meet, it flows past Fuzhou into the sea.

items.note: 西汉水，陈仓道、金牛道沿江而行，兴州、利州、阆州、合州临之。

e.note: Also called the Xihan River; the Chencang and Jinniu roads followed it, and Xingzhou, Lizhou, Langzhou and Hezhou stood on it.

items.note: 北江，经韶州南下番禺，大庾岭道的水路部分。

e.note: The Bei River, flowing south past Shaozhou to Panyu; the river section of the Dayu Pass route.

items.note: 隋唐黄河下游大致沿东汉王景所治河道，经滑州、魏州东、德州、棣州入海。今黄河下游（虚线）为 1855 年铜瓦厢改道后夺大清河入海。617 年李渊自龙门西渡黄河入关；621 年窦建德沿黄河西进救洛阳，被阻于虎牢。

e.note: In Sui and Tang times the lower Yellow River roughly followed the channel regulated by Wang Jing of the Eastern Han, flowing past Huazhou, east of Weizhou, and on past Dezhou and Dizhou to the sea. The present lower Yellow River (dashed line) took over the bed of the Daqing River to reach the sea after the 1855 course change at Tongwaxiang. In 617 Li Yuan crossed the Yellow River westward at Longmen into Guanzhong; in 621 Dou Jiande advanced west along the Yellow River to relieve Luoyang and was stopped at Hulao.

items.note: 鸭绿江，隋唐征高句丽的必经之路，国内城、乌骨城皆在其附近。

e.note: A route the Sui and Tang campaigns against Goguryeo had to take; Gungnae Fortress and Ogol Fortress both lay near it.

items.note: 黑龙江，黑水靺鞨居其下游。

e.note: The Amur; the Heishui Mohe lived on its lower course.

items.note: 额尔古纳河，室韦诸部居其两岸。

e.note: The Argun; Shiwei tribes lived on both banks.

items.note: 关中命脉。584 年隋开广通渠引渭水通漕；626 年颉利可汗兵临渭水便桥，唐太宗与之隔水对话、刑白马盟誓。

e.note: The lifeline of Guanzhong. In 584 Sui cut the Guangtong Canal, drawing on the Wei for grain transport; in 626 Illig Qaghan's army reached the Bian Bridge over the Wei, and Emperor Taizong of Tang spoke with him across the river and sealed a covenant by sacrificing a white horse.

items.note: 于阗产玉之河。

e.note: The river of Khotan that yields jade.

items.note: 流经泾州、豳州入渭，618 年浅水原之战即在泾水北岸的长武塬上。

e.note: Flowing past Jingzhou and Binzhou into the Wei; the Battle of Qianshuiyuan in 618 was fought on the Changwu tableland on the north bank of the Jing.

items.note: 流经相州、魏州一带，下游近窦建德、刘黑闼的家乡漳南县。

e.note: Flowing through the area of Xiangzhou and Weizhou; its lower course runs near Zhangnan County, home of Dou Jiande and Liu Heita.

items.note: 鄂尔浑河，突厥、薛延陀、回纥的牙帐皆在其上游一带。

e.note: The royal camps of the Turks, the Xueyantuo and the Huihe all lay around its upper reaches.

items.mod: 古济水（今黄河下游大部即其故道）
items.note: 隋唐时济水自大野泽东北流经郓、济、齐、淄、青诸州入海，又称清河；今黄河山东段即夺其故道。

e.mod: old Ji River (the lower Yellow River now runs mostly in its bed)
e.note: In Sui and Tang times the Ji flowed northeast from the Daye Marsh past Yunzhou, Jizhou, Qizhou, Zizhou and Qingzhou to the sea; it was also called the Qing River. The present Shandong section of the Yellow River has taken over its old bed.

items.note: 东都洛阳横跨洛水；617—618 年李密与王世充在洛水两岸反复争夺。

e.note: The Eastern Capital, Luoyang, straddled the Luo; in 617–618 Li Mi and Wang Shichong fought back and forth over both banks.

items.note: 流经伊阙（龙门），北魏至唐的龙门石窟开凿于此。

e.note: Flowing through Yique (Longmen), where the Longmen Grottoes were carved from the Northern Wei to the Tang.

items.note: 流经鄜、坊、同州。

e.note: Flowing past Fuzhou, Fangzhou and Tongzhou.

items.note: 流经许、陈、颍三州入淮。

e.note: Flowing through Xuzhou, Chenzhou and Yingzhou into the Huai.

items.note: 流经兖、徐、泗州入淮，徐州为泗水、汴水交汇处。

e.note: Flowing through Yanzhou, Xuzhou and Sizhou into the Huai; Xuzhou lay where the Si and Bian rivers met.

items.note: 流经恒州城南，河北中部的大河。

e.note: Flowing south of the city of Hengzhou; a major river of central Hebei.

items.note: 南阳盆地主河，于襄州入汉。

e.note: The main river of the Nanyang Basin, joining the Han at Xiangzhou.

items.note: 流经邵州入洞庭。

e.note: Flowing past Shaozhou into Dongting Lake.

items.note: 经灵渠与湘水相通。

e.note: Linked with the Xiang River by the Lingqu Canal.

items.note: 鄯州临湟水。

e.note: Shanzhou stood on the Huangshui.

items.note: 流经甘州，北入居延海。

e.note: Flowing past Ganzhou and north into Juyan Lake.

items.note: 巴尔喀什湖，西突厥游牧地的北缘，658 年后属昆陵都护府。

e.note: The northern edge of the Western Turks' grazing lands; after 658 it belonged to the Kunling Protectorate.

items.note: 贝加尔湖，骨利干居其畔，“昼长夜短，日入烹羊胛，熟，东方已明”。

e.note: The Kurykans lived on its shores, where "the days are long and the nights short; if a sheep's shoulder blade is put on to boil at sunset, by the time it is cooked the east is already light".

items.note: 唐时此处只是淮河南岸的破釜塘、白水塘等小湖，今洪泽湖为明清时形成，泗州城没于湖底。

e.note: In Tang times there were only small lakes here, such as the Pofu Pond and the Baishui Reservoir on the south bank of the Huai; today's Hongze Lake formed in the Ming and Qing, and the city of Sizhou lies sunk at its bottom.

items.note: 兴凯湖，靺鞨拂涅、号室诸部居其周边。

e.note: Lake Khanka; the Funie, Haoshi and other Mohe tribes lived around it.

items.note: 古称震泽、具区。

e.note: Anciently called Zhenze or Juqu.

items.note: 博斯腾湖，焉耆国东临此湖，644 年郭孝恪即夜渡其水奇袭焉耆。

e.note: Bosten Lake; the state of Karasahr had the lake on its eastern side, and in 644 Guo Xiaoke crossed its waters by night to take Karasahr by surprise.

items.note: 641 年文成公主入藏，松赞干布亲至柏海迎接。

e.note: In 641, when Princess Wencheng went to Tibet, Songtsen Gampo came to Baihai in person to meet her.

items.note: 641 年文成公主入藏，松赞干布亲至柏海迎接。

e.note: In 641, when Princess Wencheng went to Tibet, Songtsen Gampo came to Baihai in person to meet her.

items.note: 伊塞克湖，玄奘称“大清池”，西突厥可汗冬季牙帐在其西北的碎叶。

e.note: Called the "Great Clear Lake" by Xuanzang; the winter royal camp of the Western Turkic qaghans was at Suyab, to its northwest.

items.note: 吐谷浑都城伏俟城在湖西；609 年隋置西海郡，663 年吐蕃尽有其地。

e.note: The Tuyuhun capital, Fuqi City, stood west of the lake; Sui set up Xihai Commandery in 609, and in 663 Tibet took the whole region.

items.note: 唐称巨野泽，济水所出；944 年黄河决滑州后，河水与汶水、济水在此汇成梁山泊。

e.note: Called the Juye Marsh in Tang times, the lake from which the Ji River flowed; after the Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou in 944, its waters merged here with the Wen and Ji rivers to form the Liangshan Marsh.

items.mod: 内蒙古额济纳（今居延海）
items.note: 弱水尾闾，隋唐时属甘州境。

e.mod: Ejin Banner, Inner Mongolia (today's Juyan Lake)
e.note: The terminal lake of the Ruoshui, part of Ganzhou in Sui and Tang times.

items.note: 南中名湖，昆明诸部居其周边。

e.note: A famous lake of Nanzhong, with the Kunming tribes living around it.

items.note: 古称西洱河，洱海诸部（六诏）居其周边，664 年唐置姚州都督府。

e.note: Anciently called the Xi'er River; the Erhai tribes (Six Zhao) lived around it, and in 664 Tang set up the Yaozhou Area Command.

items.note: 镜泊湖，靺鞨居地，后为渤海上京附近。

e.note: Jingpo Lake, home of the Mohe; later near the Upper Capital of Balhae.

items.note: 河中与吐火罗的界河，玄奘称缚刍河；658 年后两岸皆为唐的羁縻府州。

e.note: The border river between Transoxiana and Tokharistan, called the Vakshu by Xuanzang; after 658 both banks were Tang loose-rein area commands and prefectures.

items.note: 石国、拔汗那临其上游，昭武九姓分布于其南。

e.note: Chach and Ferghana lay on its upper reaches, and the Sogdian states (Zhaowu) were spread to its south.

items.note: 康国（撒马尔罕）、安国（布哈拉）皆依此河。

e.note: Samarkand and Bukhara both depended on this river.

items.note: 西突厥可汗冬季牙帐碎叶城在其河畔，658 年以碎叶川为界分置昆陵、濛池二都护府。

e.note: The winter royal camp of the Western Turkic qaghans, Suyab, stood on its bank; in 658 the Kunling and Mengchi protectorates were set up with the Suyab River as their dividing line.

items.note: 西突厥游牧地，怛逻斯城临之。

e.note: Grazing land of the Western Turks; Talas City stood on it.

items.note: 612 年七月乙支文德在此半渡击隋军，三十万大军仅二千七百人生还。

e.note: In the 7th month of 612 Eulji Mundeok attacked the Sui army here as it was halfway across; of an army of 300,000, only 2,700 men got back alive.

items.note: 平壤临其右岸，隋唐水军多次沿此江进逼平壤。

e.note: Pyongyang stood on its right bank; Sui and Tang fleets repeatedly advanced up this river to threaten Pyongyang.

items.note: 百济都城泗沘、熊津皆临此江；663 年白江口之战即在其入海口。

e.note: The Baekje capitals Sabi and Ungjin both stood on this river; the Battle of Baekgang in 663 was fought at its mouth.

items.note: 五天竺的西界，玄奘曾在此渡河失落经书。

e.note: The western border of the Five Indias; Xuanzang lost scriptures here while crossing the river.

items.note: 药杀水、乌浒水的尾闾，火寻（花剌子模）在其南。

e.note: The terminal lake of the Jaxartes and the Oxus, with Khwarazm to its south.

items.note: 605 年三月炀帝发河南、淮北诸郡百余万人开凿，自洛阳西苑引谷、洛水入黄河，再自板渚引河水经汴州、宋州至盱眙入淮，渠旁筑御道、植杨柳，是隋唐漕运的生命线。

e.mod: Tongji Canal section of the Sui–Tang Grand Canal
e.note: In the 3rd month of 605 Emperor Yang called up over a million people from the commanderies of Henan and Huaibei to dig it. From the Western Park at Luoyang it led the waters of the Gu and Luo Rivers into the Yellow River, then from Banzhu led the Yellow River's water past Bianzhou and Songzhou to Xuyi, where it entered the Huai River. An imperial road was built and willows were planted along its banks. It was the lifeline of Sui and Tang grain transport.

items.note: 608 年发河北诸郡百余万人开凿，引沁水南达黄河、北通涿郡，为征高句丽转运兵粮而作；611 年炀帝自江都乘龙舟直抵涿郡。

e.note: Dug in 608 by over a million people called up from the commanderies of Hebei, it drew on the Qin River to reach the Yellow River in the south and Zhuo Commandery in the north, and was built to carry troops and grain for the Goguryeo campaigns. In 611 Emperor Yang traveled by dragon boat from Jiangdu straight to Zhuo Commandery.

items.note: 587 年隋文帝为伐陈开山阳渎，605 年炀帝发淮南十余万人重开邗沟，自山阳至扬子入江。

e.note: In 587 Emperor Wen of Sui cut the Shanyang Canal for the attack on Chen; in 605 Emperor Yang called up over 100,000 people from Huainan to reopen the Han Canal, running from Shanyang to Yangzi, where it entered the Yangtze.

items.note: 610 年开凿，自京口（润州）至余杭，长八百余里、宽十余丈，江南财赋由此北运。

e.note: Dug in 610, it ran from Jingkou (Runzhou) to Yuhang, over 800 li long and more than ten zhang wide; the wealth and taxes of Jiangnan were carried north along it.

items.note: 584 年宇文恺主持开凿的广通渠，自大兴城引渭水东至潼关，长三百余里，关中漕运得以畅通；唐称漕渠。

e.mod: south bank of the Wei between Xi'an and Tongguan
e.note: The Guangtong Canal, dug in 584 under Yuwen Kai's direction, drew water from the Wei River at Daxing City east to Tong Pass, over 300 li long, opening up grain transport for Guanzhong. In the Tang it was called the Grain Canal.

items.note: 秦凿，沟通湘水与漓水，是岭南与中原之间的水道。

e.note: Dug under the Qin, it links the Xiang River and the Li River, and was a waterway between Lingnan and the Central Plains.

items.note: 西域南北两道之间的大沙漠，玄奘东归时经其南缘，称“流沙”。

e.note: The great desert between the southern and northern routes through the Western Regions; Xuanzang passed along its southern edge on his return east and called it the "Flowing Sands".

items.note: 漠南与漠北之间的戈壁，隋唐人称大碛、沙碛；647 年唐于其间开参天可汗道。

e.note: The desert between the southern and northern steppes, called the Great Gobi (Daqi) or the Sandy Gobi (Shaqi) by Sui and Tang people; in 647 Tang opened the Road to the Heavenly Qaghan across it.

items.note: 617 年随父起兵后，李世民（598—649）几乎打满了唐朝开国的每一场硬仗：霍邑斩宋老生、入关取长安、扶风破薛仁杲；618 年浅水原灭西秦；619—620 年柏壁坚守、雀鼠谷一日八战逐刘武周；620—621 年围洛阳、虎牢一战擒窦建德降王世充；622 年洺水破刘黑闼。626 年玄武门之变后即位，645 年亲征高句丽。实线为本期行军，虚线为此前路线；路线按史籍所记地点连缀，仅为示意。

e.old: Campaign route of Li Shimin, Prince of Qin
e.note: After rising in arms with his father in 617, Li Shimin (598–649) fought in almost every hard battle of the Tang founding: Song Laosheng beheaded at Huoyi, Chang'an taken after entering Guanzhong, and Xue Rengao routed at Fufeng; Western Qin destroyed at Qianshuiyuan in 618; the stand at Baibi and the eight battles in one day at Queshu Valley that drove out Liu Wuzhou in 619–620; the siege of Luoyang in 620–621 and the single battle at Hulao that captured Dou Jiande and brought Wang Shichong's surrender; and Liu Heita defeated on the Ming River in 622. He took the throne after the Xuanwu Gate incident in 626 and led the Goguryeo campaign in person in 645. Solid lines are marches in the current period and dashed lines earlier routes; the routes join the places recorded in the sources and are only schematic.

items.note: 607 年十月屯田主事常骏、虞部主事王君政奉炀帝之命自南海郡乘舟南行，昼夜二旬至焦石山，经陵伽钵拔多洲（西与林邑相对）、师子石，望见狼牙须国之山，南达赤土之界；赤土王遣王子那邪迦随骏入贡，610 年春在弘农谒见炀帝。赤土地望诸说不一，图取马来半岛东岸说；回程时间为示意。

e.note: In the 10th month of 607 Chang Jun, secretary of the Bureau of Military Colonies, and Wang Junzheng, secretary of the Bureau of Forestry, sailed south from Nanhai Commandery on the orders of Emperor Yang. After twenty days and nights they reached Mount Jiaoshi; they passed Lingaparvata, which faces Linyi (Champa) to the west, and Shizi Rock, sighted the mountains of the state of Langkasuka, and reached the borders of Chitu in the south. The King of Chitu sent Prince Nayejia back with Chang Jun to bring tribute, and in spring 610 they were received by Emperor Yang at Hongnong. The location of Chitu is disputed; the map follows the view that it lay on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula. The timing of the return journey is schematic.

items.note: 609 年三月炀帝自长安西巡，经扶风、陇西、狄道，四月出临津关渡黄河至西平，五月围吐谷浑伏允于覆袁川，六月经大斗拔谷（今扁都口）至张掖，山路隘险，士卒冻死者太半；在燕支山观风殿大宴高昌王麴伯雅、伊吾吐屯设等二十七国使者，九月还长安。

e.note: In the 3rd month of 609 Emperor Yang set out from Chang'an on a tour of the west, passing through Fufeng, Longxi and Didao; in the 4th month he went out through the Linjin Pass and crossed the Yellow River to Xiping; in the 5th month he surrounded Fuyun of the Tuyuhun in the Fuyuan Valley; and in the 6th month he went through the Dadouba Valley (today's Biandukou) to Zhangye. The mountain road was narrow and dangerous, and more than half of the soldiers froze to death. At the Guanfeng Hall at Mount Yanzhi he held a great banquet for Qu Boya, King of Gaochang, the Tudun Shad of Yiwu and other envoys, from 27 states in all; in the 9th month he returned to Chang'an.

items.note: 629 年（一说 627 年）八月玄奘私出长安，在瓜州偷渡玉门关，经伊吾至高昌，麴文泰厚赠送行；越凌山、过热海，在素叶城见西突厥统叶护可汗，经石国、飒秣建、铁门入吐火罗，翻大雪山至迦毕试、健驮逻，633 年前后入那烂陀寺，从戒贤受学五年，又遍游五天竺；642 年为戒日王曲女城大会论主，643 年东归，翻葱岭经佉沙、于阗，645 年正月回到长安，二月在洛阳谒见太宗。在印度的行程年份诸说不一，图取通行说，中间各点为示意。

e.old: Xuanzang's journey west in search of the Dharma
e.note: In the 8th month of 629 (or 627) Xuanzang left Chang'an without permission. At Guazhou he slipped secretly past Yumen Pass, and went by way of Yiwu to Gaochang, where Qu Wentai gave him rich gifts and saw him on his way. He crossed the Ling Mountains, passed Issyk-Kul and met Tong Yabghu Qaghan of the Western Turks at Suyab; by way of Chach, Samarkand and the Iron Gate he entered Tokharistan, and crossed the Great Snow Mountains to Kapisa and Gandhara. Around 633 he entered Nalanda Monastery, where he studied under Silabhadra for five years, and he also traveled throughout the Five Indias. In 642 he was the chief debater at Harsha's great assembly at Kanyakubja. In 643 he set out for home, crossing the Pamirs and passing through Kashgar and Khotan; he returned to Chang'an in the 1st month of 645, and in the 2nd month he was received by Taizong at Luoyang. The dates of his travels in India vary among the sources; the map follows the commonly accepted account, and the intermediate points are schematic.

items.note: 630 年正月李靖率骁骑三千自马邑出恶阳岭，夜袭定襄，颉利可汗惊走碛口；李勣出云中，破突厥于白道；颉利退保铁山，遣使请降，二月李靖与李勣会于白道，乘唐使安抚之际以万骑掩袭，大破其牙帐于阴山，三月颉利被擒，东突厥亡。

e.old: Li Jing destroys the Eastern Turks in a surprise attack
e.note: In the 1st month of 630 Li Jing led 3,000 picked horsemen out from Mayi through the Eyang Pass and made a night attack on Dingxiang; Illig Qaghan fled in alarm to Qikou. Li Ji came out from Yunzhong and defeated the Turks at Baidao. Illig fell back to hold Tieshan and sent envoys asking to surrender. In the 2nd month Li Jing and Li Ji joined forces at Baidao and, while a Tang envoy was there to reassure Illig, made a surprise attack with 10,000 horsemen and crushed his royal camp in the Yin Mountains; in the 3rd month Illig was captured, and the Eastern Turkic Qaghanate fell.

items.note: 639 年十二月以侯君集为交河道行军大总管，率步骑数万讨高昌；640 年八月唐军出碛口至柳谷，麴文泰惊惧病死，唐军先下田地城，进围高昌，麴智盛出降，唐以其地置西州，九月于交河城置安西都护府。

e.note: In the 12th month of 639 Hou Junji was made commander-in-chief of the Jiaohe Route expedition and led tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against Gaochang. In the 8th month of 640 the Tang army came out at the edge of the desert and reached Liugu; Qu Wentai fell ill from fear and died. The Tang army first took Tiandi City and then besieged Gaochang, and Qu Zhisheng came out and surrendered. Tang made the territory into Xizhou, and in the 9th month set up the Anxi Protectorate at Jiaohe City.

items.note: 641 年正月文成公主由江夏王李道宗护送出长安，循唐蕃古道经鄯州、赤岭、大非川，松赞干布率兵至柏海（河源）亲迎，行子婿之礼，同归逻些。中间各点与到达时间为示意。

e.note: In the 1st month of 641 Princess Wencheng left Chang'an, escorted by Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, and followed the old Tang–Tibet road by way of Shanzhou, Chiling and Dafeichuan. Songtsen Gampo led troops to Baihai (the source of the Yellow River) to meet her in person and performed the rites of a son-in-law, and they returned together to Rasa. The intermediate points and the arrival date are schematic.

items.note: 647 年王玄策、蒋师仁出使天竺，适逢戒日王卒、阿罗那顺篡立，发兵劫掠使团；玄策脱身奔吐蕃西境，檄召吐蕃兵千二百人、泥婆罗兵七千余骑，648 年五月大破阿罗那顺于茶镈和罗城，擒之献于长安。往返道路取吐蕃—泥婆罗道，时间为示意。

e.old: Wang Xuance's second mission to India
e.note: In 647 Wang Xuance and Jiang Shiren went as envoys to India just as Harsha died and Arunasva usurped the throne; Arunasva sent troops to plunder the mission. Wang Xuance escaped to the western border of Tibet and called up 1,200 Tibetan troops and over 7,000 Nepalese cavalry; in the 5th month of 648 he crushed Arunasva at Tirabhukti, captured him and presented him at Chang'an. The route there and back is drawn along the Tibet–Nepal road, and the dates are schematic.

items.note: 657 年闰正月以苏定方为伊丽道行军大总管，发回纥等兵自北道讨阿史那贺鲁（阿史那弥射、步真自南道招集旧众）；十二月至金山北，先破处木昆部，又大破贺鲁十万众于曳咥河，追至双河，又进至碎叶水，尽收其众；贺鲁奔石国，被石国人执送萧嗣业。中间各点与到达时间为示意。

e.old: Su Dingfang destroys the Western Turks
e.note: In the intercalary 1st month of 657 Su Dingfang was made commander-in-chief of the Ili Route expedition and, with troops raised from the Huihe (Uyghurs) and others, marched by the northern route against Ashina Helu (Ashina Mishe and Buzhen gathered their former followers by the southern route). In the 12th month he reached the area north of the Altai and first defeated the Chumukun tribe, then crushed Helu's 100,000 men on the Irtysh, pursued him to Shuanghe and advanced on to the Suyab River, taking over all his people. Helu fled to Chach, where the people of Chach seized him and handed him over to Xiao Siye. The intermediate points and arrival dates are schematic.

items.note: 660 年三月以苏定方为神丘道大总管，率水陆十三万自成山渡海，六月二十一日至德物岛，新罗太子金法敏率兵船百艘来迎；七月金庾信于黄山之原破阶伯，唐军自伎伐浦溯白江，与新罗军会于泗沘城下，破之，义慈王自熊津出降，百济亡。十一月苏定方献俘于东都则天门。

e.note: In the 3rd month of 660 Su Dingfang was made commander-in-chief of the Shenqiu Route and led 130,000 land and naval troops across the sea from Chengshan. On the 21st day of the 6th month he reached Deongmul Island, where Kim Beop-min, Crown Prince of Silla, came to meet him with 100 warships. In the 7th month Kim Yu-sin defeated Gyebaek at Hwangsanbeol, while the Tang army sailed up the Baek River from Gibeolpo, joined the Silla army beneath the walls of Sabi and took the city; King Uija came out of Ungjin and surrendered, and Baekje fell. In the 11th month Su Dingfang presented his captives at the Zetian Gate of the Eastern Capital.

items.note: 666 年十二月以李勣为辽东道行军大总管；667 年二月渡辽，九月拔新城；668 年二月薛仁贵拔扶余城，李勣会诸军进逼鸭绿栅，九月与新罗军合围平壤，泉男建部将开门内应，擒宝藏王，高句丽亡。十二月李勣献俘于含元殿。

e.note: In the 12th month of 666 Li Ji was made commander-in-chief of the Liaodong Route expedition. In the 2nd month of 667 he crossed the Liao River, and in the 9th month he took Sinseong. In the 2nd month of 668 Xue Rengui stormed Buyeo Fortress, and Li Ji joined forces with the other armies and pressed on to the Yalu Stockade; in the 9th month, together with the Silla army, he surrounded Pyongyang. An officer of Yeon Namgeon opened the gates from within, King Bojang was captured, and Goguryeo fell. In the 12th month Li Ji presented his captives at the Hanyuan Hall.

items.note: 679 年裴行俭以册送波斯王子泥涅师归国为名西行，至西州召四镇诸蕃酋长子弟千余人随行，佯言校猎，倍道而进，突至西突厥阿史那都支牙帐，擒都支，又擒李遮匐；留王方翼筑碎叶城，自押二人还朝。

e.note: In 679 Pei Xingjian traveled west on the pretext of escorting the Persian prince Narseh home to be installed as king. At Xizhou he summoned over 1,000 sons and younger brothers of the chieftains of the peoples of the Four Garrisons to go with him; giving out that he was going hunting, he pressed on at double speed and suddenly arrived at the royal camp of Ashina Duzhi of the Western Turks. He captured Duzhi, and then Li Zhefu as well. He left Wang Fangyi to build the city of Suyab and himself escorted the two prisoners back to court.

items.note: 671 年十一月义净在广州搭波斯商舶南行，二十日至室利佛逝，停六月学声明，经末罗瑜、羯荼、裸人国，673 年二月至东印度耽摩立底，675 年起在那烂陀寺求学约十年；685 年东返，在室利佛逝译经著述，689 年一度回广州延请助手，695 年五月携梵本经律论约四百部至洛阳，武则天亲迎于上东门外。著有《大唐西域求法高僧传》《南海寄归内法传》。

e.old: Yijing's sea journey in search of the Dharma
e.note: In the 11th month of 671 Yijing sailed south from Guangzhou on a Persian merchant ship. After 20 days he reached Srivijaya, where he stayed six months to study Sanskrit grammar; then, by way of Malayu, Kedah and the Land of the Naked People, he reached Tamralipti in eastern India in the 2nd month of 673. From 675 he studied at Nalanda Monastery for about ten years. In 685 he set out back east and translated scriptures and wrote at Srivijaya; in 689 he went back to Guangzhou for a time to recruit assistants. In the 5th month of 695 he arrived at Luoyang with some 400 Sanskrit texts of sutras, vinaya and treatises, and Wu Zetian came in person to welcome him outside the Shangdong Gate. He wrote the Da Tang xiyu qiufa gaoseng zhuan and the Nanhai jigui neifa zhuan.

items.note: 747 年高仙芝以行营节度使率步骑一万自安西出发，经拨换城、握瑟德、疏勒、葱岭守捉、播密川至特勒满川（五识匿），分兵三道，七月十三日会攻吐蕃连云堡，越坦驹岭，入阿弩越城，进至小勃律都城孽多，擒其王及吐蕃公主，斩断娑夷河藤桥以绝吐蕃援兵，九月复至连云堡，班师。

e.old: Gao Xianzhi's expedition to Little Balur
e.note: In 747 Gao Xianzhi, as military governor of the field army, set out from Anxi with 10,000 infantry and cavalry. By way of Bohuan City, Wosede, Kashgar, Congling Garrison and the Pamir Valley he reached the Teleman Valley (the Five Shighnan), where he divided his forces into three columns; on the 13th day of the 7th month they converged on the Tibetan stronghold of Lianyun Fort. He crossed the Darkot Pass, entered Anuyue City and advanced to Gilgit, the capital of Little Balur, capturing its king and the Tibetan princess. He cut the rattan bridge over the Suoyi River to keep out Tibetan relief forces, and in the 9th month he was back at Lianyun Fort and led his army home.

items.note: 751 年石国王子引大食兵欲攻四镇，高仙芝率蕃汉兵三万先发，越拔达岭深入七百余里至怛罗斯城，与大食军相持五日，葛逻禄部众倒戈，唐军大败，仙芝收余众夜遁，归安西。中间各点与到达时间为示意。

e.note: In 751 the prince of Chach brought in troops of the Arab Caliphate, intending to attack the Four Garrisons. Gao Xianzhi struck first with 30,000 tribal and Han troops, crossing the Bedel Pass and pushing over 700 li deep to the city of Talas, where he faced the Caliphate army for five days. The Karluks changed sides, and the Tang army was heavily defeated; Gao Xianzhi gathered the survivors and slipped away by night, returning to Anxi. The intermediate points and arrival dates are schematic.

items.note: 鉴真受日本僧荣叡、普照之请，五次东渡未成，双目失明。753 年十月十九日离扬州，十一月十六日随遣唐使藤原清河、吉备真备船队自黄泗浦出海，二十一日至阿儿奈波岛（冲绳），十二月七日至益救岛（屋久岛），二十日在萨摩秋妻屋浦登岸，经大宰府，754 年二月四日入平城京，在东大寺设坛传戒，后建唐招提寺。

e.note: At the invitation of the Japanese monks Yōei and Fushō, Jianzhen made five attempts to cross east, all without success, and lost the sight of both eyes. He left Yangzhou on the 19th day of the 10th month of 753, and on the 16th day of the 11th month put out to sea from Huangsipu with the fleet of the envoys to Tang, Fujiwara no Kiyokawa and Kibi no Makibi. On the 21st he reached Okinawa Island, on the 7th day of the 12th month Yakushima, and on the 20th he landed at Akimeya-ura in Satsuma. By way of Dazaifu he entered Heijō-kyō on the 4th day of the 2nd month of 754, set up an ordination platform at Tōdai-ji to confer the precepts, and later built Tōshōdai-ji.

items.note: 薛延陀、回纥、仆骨、同罗、拔野古等十余部，游牧漠北，役属突厥，627 年联合叛离。

e.note: Over ten tribes, including the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Pugu, Tongluo and Bayegu, who roamed north of the Gobi as subjects of the Turks and broke away together in 627.

items.mod: 蒙古色楞格河—鄂尔浑河
items.note: 铁勒之一，646 年与唐夹击薛延陀，647 年为瀚海都督府，后来成为漠北霸主（回鹘）。

e.note: One of the Tiele; in 646 it joined Tang in a pincer attack on the Xueyantuo, in 647 it became the Hanhai Area Command, and it later became the dominant power north of the Gobi (as the Huihu).

items.note: 坚昆，“人皆长大，赤发、皙面、绿瞳”，648 年入朝，置坚昆都督府。

e.note: Also Jiankun; "the people are all tall, with red hair, fair faces and green eyes". They came to court in 648, and the Jiankun Area Command was set up.

items.note: 铁勒最北之部，647 年遣使献马，唐以其地为玄阙州。

e.note: The northernmost of the Tiele tribes; they sent envoys with horses in 647, and Tang made their land Xuanque Zhou.

items.mod: 新疆巴里坤—吉木萨尔一带
items.note: 西突厥别部，后来的沙陀即出于此。

e.note: A separate branch of the Western Turks, from which the later Shatuo came.

items.note: 突厥别部，居金山西南，657 年后隶唐。

e.note: A separate branch of the Turks, living southwest of the Altai; under Tang from 657.

items.note: 铁勒之一，居贪汗山北，632 年首领契苾何力率众内附，迁居甘、凉之间。

e.note: One of the Tiele, living north of Mount Tanhan; in 632 their chief Qibi Heli led his people to submit to the empire, and they were moved to lands between Ganzhou and Liangzhou.

items.note: 拓跋氏等党项诸部，635 年后多内附为唐羁縻州，西部为吐蕃所并。

e.note: The Tangut tribes, including the Tuoba; after 635 most of them submitted to the empire as Tang loose-rein prefectures, while the western ones were absorbed by Tibet.

items.note: 663 年国亡后诺曷钵率残部数千帐奔凉州，唐置安乐州于灵州安置。

e.note: After the state fell in 663, Nuohebo fled to Liangzhou with a remnant of several thousand tents; Tang set up Anle Zhou at Lingzhou to resettle them.

items.note: 672 年二月诺曷钵率部自凉州先徙鄯州浩亹水南，寻徙灵州，唐以鸣沙县地置安乐州，以诺曷钵为刺史；至德后安乐州陷吐蕃，残部东徙，散处朔方、河东。

e.note: In the 2nd month of 672 Nuohebo led his people from Liangzhou, first to the south of the Haomen River in Shanzhou and soon after to Lingzhou; Tang set up Anle Zhou on the land of Mingsha County and made Nuohebo its prefect. After the Zhide era Anle Zhou fell to Tibet, and the remnants moved east and scattered over Shuofang and Hedong.

items.mod: 内蒙古鄂托克前旗一带
items.note: 679 年于灵、夏南境以降突厥中的粟特部众置鲁、丽、含、塞、依、契六州，号六胡州；721—722 年康待宾、康愿子相继起事，平定后徙其众五万余口于中原，738 年置宥州安置还归者。

e.mod: around Otog Front Banner, Inner Mongolia
e.note: In 679 Tang set up six prefectures on the southern borders of Lingzhou and Xiazhou for the Sogdians among the surrendered Turks: Luzhou, Lizhou, Hanzhou, Saizhou, Yizhou and Qizhou, called the Six Hu Prefectures. In 721–722 Kang Daibin and Kang Yuanzi rose one after the other; after they were put down, over 50,000 of their people were moved to the Central Plains, and in 738 Tang set up Youzhou to resettle those who returned.

items.note: 巴蜀南部山地的獠人，隋唐时屡有反抗。

e.note: The Lao people of the mountains of southern Ba and Shu, who repeatedly resisted in Sui and Tang times.

items.note: 岭南土著，以冼夫人、冯盎家族为首领。

e.note: Natives of Lingnan, led by the family of Lady Xian and Feng Ang.

items.note: 武陵山区的蛮族，散居五溪之间。

e.note: Tribes of the Wuling mountain region, scattered among the Five Streams.

items.note: 南中诸族，与白蛮杂居，爨氏统之。

e.note: Peoples of Nanzhong living intermixed with the Baiman, under the rule of the Cuan clan.

items.note: 《隋书》有《流求国传》，610 年陈稜率军渡海击之。

e.note: The Book of Sui has an "Account of Liuqiu"; in 610 Chen Leng led an army across the sea to attack it.

items.note: 女王国苏毗，7 世纪初被吐蕃征服，成为吐蕃的重要组成部分。

e.note: Sumpa, the Women's Kingdom, was conquered by Tibet in the early 7th century and became an important part of Tibet.

items.note: 嚈哒（白匈奴）560 年代被突厥、波斯夹击灭亡，余众散居吐火罗诸地。

e.note: The Hephthalites (White Huns) were destroyed in the 560s by a pincer attack from the Turks and Persia; their remnants scattered across the lands of Tokharistan.
